prompt:
--- Design document ---
Checkout payment flow (design doc)

When a customer places order o1, the checkout service (the client) sends a charge request to an
external payment provider and waits for the reply. The network between them is unreliable: a request
or a response can be lost, and messages can be delayed arbitrarily, so a request may still be in
transit after the client has stopped waiting for it. The provider serves requests concurrently on
several worker threads, in whatever order they arrive, so the steps of different requests (looking up
records, charging, writing records) can interleave.

Each request is one attempt (a0 for the first try). After sending an attempt the client starts a
timer at t0; every clock tick advances it by one, and when it reaches t15 (15 ticks after sending)
without a response the client gives up on that attempt and retries with the next attempt number
(a1, then a2). At most two retries are made. If a success response arrives while the client is still
waiting, the order is confirmed and no further attempts are made.

Charging and duplicate protection. Every attempt for an order carries the same idempotency key
(derived from the order number). When a request arrives, the provider looks the key up and, in the
same atomic database operation, inserts a reservation if it is absent (an insert-if-absent with a
unique constraint). Only a request whose insert succeeded is approved and charged; when the charge
succeeds the reservation is completed with the stored response. A request whose key already has a
completed record gets the stored success response back without a new charge; a request that finds
only an unfinished reservation is not charged either.

Initially the client is about to send attempt a0 for order o1; nothing has been charged and the provider has no record for o1.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
(define (domain payments)
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types order attempt tick)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts: exactly one deduplication mode holds ---
    (dedup-none)     ; the provider does not deduplicate requests
    (dedup-atomic)   ; the provider looks up and reserves the idempotency key in one atomic step
    (dedup-racy)     ; the provider looks up the key, but only records it after the charge succeeds
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-attempt ?a ?b - attempt)   ; attempt ?b is the retry that follows attempt ?a
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick)         ; timer value ?u follows ?t
    (first-tick ?t - tick)           ; timer value right after a request is sent
    (timeout-tick ?t - tick)         ; timer value at which the client gives up waiting
    ;; --- client ---
    (ready ?o - order ?a - attempt)    ; client is about to send attempt ?a for order ?o
    (waiting ?o - order ?a - attempt)  ; client sent attempt ?a and awaits the response
    (clock ?o - order ?t - tick)       ; client's timer for the outstanding attempt
    (confirmed ?o - order)             ; client received a success response
    ;; --- network ---
    (in-flight ?o - order ?a - attempt) ; request of attempt ?a travelling to the provider
    (response ?o - order)               ; success response travelling back to the client
    ;; --- provider ---
    (approved ?o - order ?a - attempt)  ; provider accepted attempt ?a and will charge it
    (no-record ?o - order)              ; no idempotency record (and no reservation) for ?o yet
    (record ?o - order)                 ; idempotency record for ?o stored
    (uncharged ?o - order)
    (charged ?o - order)                ; card charged once
    (charged-twice ?o - order))         ; card charged a second time (the violation)

  (:action send
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (ready ?o ?a) (first-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (ready ?o ?a)) (waiting ?o ?a) (in-flight ?o ?a) (clock ?o ?t)))
  (:action lose-request
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (in-flight ?o ?a)
    :effect (not (in-flight ?o ?a)))
  (:action accept-no-dedup
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-none) (in-flight ?o ?a))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action accept-new-atomic
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-atomic) (in-flight ?o ?a) (no-record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (not (no-record ?o)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action accept-new-racy
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-racy) (in-flight ?o ?a) (no-record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action replay-duplicate-atomic
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-atomic) (in-flight ?o ?a) (record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (response ?o)))
  (:action replay-duplicate-racy
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-racy) (in-flight ?o ?a) (record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (response ?o)))
  (:action charge
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (approved ?o ?a) (uncharged ?o))
    :effect (and (not (approved ?o ?a)) (not (uncharged ?o)) (not (no-record ?o))
                 (charged ?o) (record ?o) (response ?o)))
  (:action charge-again
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (approved ?o ?a) (charged ?o))
    :effect (and (not (approved ?o ?a)) (charged-twice ?o) (response ?o)))
  (:action lose-response
    :parameters (?o - order)
    :precondition (response ?o)
    :effect (not (response ?o)))
  (:action receive-response
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (waiting ?o ?a) (response ?o))
    :effect (and (not (waiting ?o ?a)) (not (response ?o)) (confirmed ?o)))
  (:action tick
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt ?t ?u - tick)
    :precondition (and (waiting ?o ?a) (clock ?o ?t) (next-tick ?t ?u))
    :effect (and (not (clock ?o ?t)) (clock ?o ?u)))
  (:action time-out-and-retry
    :parameters (?o - order ?a ?b - attempt ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (waiting ?o ?a) (clock ?o ?t) (timeout-tick ?t) (next-attempt ?a ?b))
    :effect (and (not (waiting ?o ?a)) (not (clock ?o ?t)) (ready ?o ?b))))
```

system: You are a formal-methods engineer. You translate design documents into precise PDDL planning problems that a classical planner can analyse.
prompt:
--- Design document ---
Payout worker: queue consumer design (design doc)

When a seller's balance is settled, a "send payout" message (m1) is put on a message queue. A
consumer process (w1) receives messages from the queue and, for each one, performs the payout by
crediting the amount to the seller's wallet balance, which is stored in the payments database (a
credit, once committed, is not reversed automatically), then acknowledges the message so the queue
deletes it.

The queue guarantees at-least-once delivery. A received message is hidden from consumers; if it is
not acknowledged within 11 clock ticks of being received (the visibility timeout) it becomes visible
again and will be delivered again. The consumer process can crash at any moment and is restarted
automatically, after which it continues receiving messages.

Processing and deduplication. The consumer records the ids of messages it has already paid out in a
table in the payments database. The wallet credit and the id record are written in the same database
transaction, so either both are stored or neither is (a crash before the commit rolls both back).
Before performing a payout the consumer checks the table: if the id is there it skips the payout and
only acknowledges the message.

Initially m1 is in the queue and visible, nothing has been paid out, and w1 is idle.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
(define (domain queue)
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types message consumer tick)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts: exactly one deduplication mode holds ---
    (dedup-none)      ; the consumer processes every delivery
    (dedup-durable)   ; processed ids are recorded in the database, atomically with the side effect
    (dedup-memory)    ; processed ids are recorded in an in-memory set of the consumer process
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick) (zero-tick ?t - tick)
    (visibility-timeout ?t - tick)        ; age at which an unacknowledged message becomes visible again
    ;; --- queue ---
    (in-queue ?m - message) (visible ?m - message) (hidden ?m - message ?t - tick) (acked ?m - message)
    ;; --- consumer ---
    (idle ?w - consumer) (working ?w - consumer ?m - message) (handled ?w - consumer ?m - message)
    ;; --- effects of processing ---
    (unprocessed ?m - message) (processed ?m - message) (processed-twice ?m - message)
    (not-seen ?m - message) (seen ?m - message))

  (:action receive
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (idle ?w) (visible ?m) (in-queue ?m) (zero-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (idle ?w)) (not (visible ?m)) (working ?w ?m) (hidden ?m ?t)))
  (:action process-without-dedup
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (dedup-none) (working ?w ?m) (unprocessed ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (not (unprocessed ?m)) (processed ?m) (handled ?w ?m)))
  (:action process-and-record-durably
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (dedup-durable) (working ?w ?m) (unprocessed ?m) (not-seen ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (not (unprocessed ?m)) (not (not-seen ?m)) (seen ?m)
                 (processed ?m) (handled ?w ?m)))
  (:action process-and-record-in-memory
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (dedup-memory) (working ?w ?m) (unprocessed ?m) (not-seen ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (not (unprocessed ?m)) (not (not-seen ?m)) (seen ?m)
                 (processed ?m) (handled ?w ?m)))
  (:action skip-duplicate
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (working ?w ?m) (seen ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (handled ?w ?m)))
  (:action process-again
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (working ?w ?m) (processed ?m) (not-seen ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (processed-twice ?m) (handled ?w ?m)))
  (:action ack
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (handled ?w ?m) (hidden ?m ?t))
    :effect (and (not (handled ?w ?m)) (not (hidden ?m ?t)) (not (in-queue ?m)) (idle ?w) (acked ?m)))
  (:action tick
    :parameters (?m - message ?t ?u - tick)
    :precondition (and (hidden ?m ?t) (next-tick ?t ?u))
    :effect (and (not (hidden ?m ?t)) (hidden ?m ?u)))
  (:action reappear
    :parameters (?m - message ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (hidden ?m ?t) (visibility-timeout ?t) (in-queue ?m))
    :effect (and (not (hidden ?m ?t)) (visible ?m)))
  (:action crash-restart
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (handled ?w ?m)
    :effect (and (not (handled ?w ?m)) (idle ?w)))
  (:action crash-restart-losing-memory
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (dedup-memory) (handled ?w ?m) (seen ?m))
    :effect (and (not (handled ?w ?m)) (not (seen ?m)) (not-seen ?m) (idle ?w))))
```

```python
def largest_proper_divisor(n):
    """Return the largest integer d with 1 <= d < n that divides `n` exactly.
    """
    best = 1
    for d in range(1, n):
        if n % d != 0:
            best = d
    return best
```

Question: is there a valid input for which the function does NOT behave as its docstring specifies (it returns a different value, or raises an exception)?

completion.text:
The function sets `best = d` whenever `n % d != 0`, which is the opposite of the condition it needs: it tracks the largest non-divisor, not the largest divisor.

Take n = 6. The proper divisors are 1, 2 and 3, so the docstring requires 3. The loop runs over d = 1..5:
- d=1: 6%1 == 0, no update.
- d=2: divides, no update.
- d=3: divides, no update.
- d=4: 6%4 = 2 != 0, so best = 4.
- d=5: 6%5 = 1 != 0, so best = 5.

The function returns 5 instead of 3.

A smaller case also fails. For n = 2, the loop only visits d=1, which divides 2, so best stays 1. That is correct, so n = 2 does not expose the bug, but n = 6 does.

```json
{"verdict": "bug", "failing_input": {"n": 6}, "expected": 3, "actual": 5}
```

--- Design document ---
Checkout payment flow (design doc)

When a customer places order o1, the checkout service (the client) sends a charge request to an
external payment provider and waits for the reply. The network between them is unreliable: a request
or a response can be lost, and messages can be delayed arbitrarily, so a request may still be in
transit after the client has stopped waiting for it. The provider handles requests one at a time,
in whatever order they arrive.

Each request is one attempt (a0 for the first try). After sending an attempt the client starts a
timer at t0; every clock tick advances it by one, and when it reaches t15 (15 ticks after sending)
without a response the client gives up on that attempt and retries with the next attempt number
(a1, then a2). At most two retries are made. If a success response arrives while the client is still
waiting, the order is confirmed and no further attempts are made.

Charging. The provider treats every request it receives as a new payment: it approves the request
and charges the customer's card, then sends a success response. Requests carry the order number for
bookkeeping only; the provider does not use it to detect repeats.

Initially the client is about to send attempt a0 for order o1; nothing has been charged and the provider has no record for o1.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
(define (domain payments)
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types order attempt tick)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts: exactly one deduplication mode holds ---
    (dedup-none)     ; the provider does not deduplicate requests
    (dedup-atomic)   ; the provider looks up and reserves the idempotency key in one atomic step
    (dedup-racy)     ; the provider looks up the key, but only records it after the charge succeeds
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-attempt ?a ?b - attempt)   ; attempt ?b is the retry that follows attempt ?a
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick)         ; timer value ?u follows ?t
    (first-tick ?t - tick)           ; timer value right after a request is sent
    (timeout-tick ?t - tick)         ; timer value at which the client gives up waiting
    ;; --- client ---
    (ready ?o - order ?a - attempt)    ; client is about to send attempt ?a for order ?o
    (waiting ?o - order ?a - attempt)  ; client sent attempt ?a and awaits the response
    (clock ?o - order ?t - tick)       ; client's timer for the outstanding attempt
    (confirmed ?o - order)             ; client received a success response
    ;; --- network ---
    (in-flight ?o - order ?a - attempt) ; request of attempt ?a travelling to the provider
    (response ?o - order)               ; success response travelling back to the client
    ;; --- provider ---
    (approved ?o - order ?a - attempt)  ; provider accepted attempt ?a and will charge it
    (no-record ?o - order)              ; no idempotency record (and no reservation) for ?o yet
    (record ?o - order)                 ; idempotency record for ?o stored
    (uncharged ?o - order)
    (charged ?o - order)                ; card charged once
    (charged-twice ?o - order))         ; card charged a second time (the violation)

  (:action send
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (ready ?o ?a) (first-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (ready ?o ?a)) (waiting ?o ?a) (in-flight ?o ?a) (clock ?o ?t)))
  (:action lose-request
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (in-flight ?o ?a)
    :effect (not (in-flight ?o ?a)))
  (:action accept-no-dedup
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-none) (in-flight ?o ?a))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action accept-new-atomic
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-atomic) (in-flight ?o ?a) (no-record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (not (no-record ?o)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action accept-new-racy
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-racy) (in-flight ?o ?a) (no-record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action replay-duplicate-atomic
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-atomic) (in-flight ?o ?a) (record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (response ?o)))
  (:action replay-duplicate-racy
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-racy) (in-flight ?o ?a) (record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (response ?o)))
  (:action charge
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (approved ?o ?a) (uncharged ?o))
    :effect (and (not (approved ?o ?a)) (not (uncharged ?o)) (not (no-record ?o))

  (:action charge-again
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (approved ?o ?a) (charged ?o))
    :effect (and (not (approved ?o ?a)) (charged-twice ?o) (response ?o)))
  (:action lose-response
    :parameters (?o - order)
    :precondition (response ?o)
    :effect (not (response ?o)))
  (:action receive-response
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (waiting ?o ?a) (response ?o))
    :effect (and (not (waiting ?o ?a)) (not (response ?o)) (confirmed ?o)))
  (:action tick
```

--- Design document ---
Checkout payment flow (design doc)

When a customer places order o1, the checkout service (the client) sends a charge request to an
external payment provider and waits for the reply. The network between them is unreliable: a request
or a response can be lost, and messages can be delayed arbitrarily, so a request may still be in
transit after the client has stopped waiting for it. The provider serves requests concurrently on
several worker threads, in whatever order they arrive, so the steps of different requests (looking up
records, charging, writing records) can interleave.

Each request is one attempt (a0 for the first try). After sending an attempt the client starts a
timer at t0; every clock tick advances it by one, and when it reaches t31 (31 ticks after sending)
without a response the client gives up on that attempt and retries with the next attempt number
(a1, then a2). At most two retries are made. If a success response arrives while the client is still
waiting, the order is confirmed and no further attempts are made.

Charging and duplicate protection. Every attempt for an order carries the same idempotency key
(derived from the order number). When a request arrives, the provider looks the key up in its
idempotency table. If a record is found, the provider does not charge again; it just returns the
stored success response. If no record is found, the provider approves the request, charges the card,
and, once the charge has succeeded, writes the record for the key together with the response.

Initially the client is about to send attempt a0 for order o1; nothing has been charged and the provider has no record for o1.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types order attempt tick)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts: exactly one deduplication mode holds ---
    (dedup-none)     ; the provider does not deduplicate requests
    (dedup-atomic)   ; the provider looks up and reserves the idempotency key in one atomic step
    (dedup-racy)     ; the provider looks up the key, but only records it after the charge succeeds
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-attempt ?a ?b - attempt)   ; attempt ?b is the retry that follows attempt ?a
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick)         ; timer value ?u follows ?t
    (first-tick ?t - tick)           ; timer value right after a request is sent
    (timeout-tick ?t - tick)         ; timer value at which the client gives up waiting
    ;; --- client ---
    (ready ?o - order ?a - attempt)    ; client is about to send attempt ?a for order ?o
    (waiting ?o - order ?a - attempt)  ; client sent attempt ?a and awaits the response
    (clock ?o - order ?t - tick)       ; client's timer for the outstanding attempt
    (confirmed ?o - order)             ; client received a success response
    ;; --- network ---
    (in-flight ?o - order ?a - attempt) ; request of attempt ?a travelling to the provider
    (response ?o - order)               ; success response travelling back to the client
    ;; --- provider ---
    (approved ?o - order ?a - attempt)  ; provider accepted attempt ?a and will charge it

    (record ?o - order)                 ; idempotency record for ?o stored
    (uncharged ?o - order)
    (charged ?o - order)                ; card charged once
    (charged-twice ?o - order))         ; card charged a second time (the violation)

    :precondition (and (ready ?o ?a) (first-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (ready ?o ?a)) (waiting ?o ?a) (in-flight ?o ?a) (clock ?o ?t)))

    :precondition (in-flight ?o ?a)
    :effect (not (in-flight ?o ?a)))

    :precondition (and (dedup-none) (in-flight ?o ?a))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (approved ?o ?a)))

    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (not (no-record ?o)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action accept-new-racy

    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action replay-duplicate-atomic

    :precondition (and (dedup-atomic) (in-flight ?o ?a) (record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (response ?o)))

    :precondition (and (dedup-racy) (in-flight ?o ?a) (record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (response ?o)))
  (:action charge

    :precondition (and (approved ?o ?a) (uncharged ?o))
    :effect (and (not (approved ?o ?a)) (not (uncharged ?o)) (not (no-record ?o))
```

```python
def can_split_evenly(xs):
    """Return True if the values in `xs` can be divided into two groups with equal sums,
    each value going to exactly one of the groups (a group may be empty), and False
    otherwise.
    """
    total = sum(xs)
    if total % 2 == 1:
        return False
    target = total // 2
    reachable = [True] + [False] * target
    for x in xs:
        for s in range(target, x, -1):
            if reachable[s - x]:
                reachable[s] = True
    return reachable[target]
```

completion.text:
The inner loop is `range(target, x, -1)`, which runs `s` from `target` down to `x + 1`. It never reaches `s == x`. That is the case where a single element `x` is added to the empty subset (`reachable[0]`) to make sum `x`. The standard 0/1 knapsack loop needs `range(target, x - 1, -1)`.

Sums of exactly `x` can therefore only be built through a previously reachable nonzero sum, never from zero.

Trace for `xs = [2, 2]`:
- `total = 4`, `target = 2`, `reachable = [True, False, False]`.
- For the first `x = 2`, `range(2, 2, -1)` is empty, so nothing changes.
- The second `x = 2` is the same.
- The function returns `reachable[2]`, which is `False`.

The docstring requires `True`, since the groups `[2]` and `[2]` have equal sums.

--- Design document ---
Checkout payment flow (design doc)

When a customer places order o1, the checkout service (the client) sends a charge request to an
external payment provider and waits for the reply. The network between them is unreliable: a request
or a response can be lost, and messages can be delayed arbitrarily, so a request may still be in
transit after the client has stopped waiting for it. The provider serves requests concurrently on
several worker threads, in whatever order they arrive, so the steps of different requests (looking up
records, charging, writing records) can interleave.

Each request is one attempt (a0 for the first try). After sending an attempt the client starts a
timer at t0; every clock tick advances it by one, and when it reaches t3 (3 ticks after sending)
without a response the client gives up on that attempt and retries with the next attempt number
(a1, then a2). At most two retries are made. If a success response arrives while the client is still
waiting, the order is confirmed and no further attempts are made.

Charging and duplicate protection. Every attempt for an order carries the same idempotency key
(derived from the order number). When a request arrives, the provider looks the key up in its
idempotency table. If a record is found, the provider does not charge again; it just returns the

**Event sequence**

Report-generation job: leader lock design (design doc)

Two worker processes, c1 and c2, may both try to run the nightly job, which overwrites a shared file
in object storage. To make sure only one of them writes, a worker must first acquire a lock from the
lock service. The lock is a lease: it is granted for 3 clock ticks, after which the lock service
considers it expired and may grant it to the other worker. Each grant comes with a token from a
counter (k1 for the first grant, then k2, ...; k0 is the initial counter value and is never handed
out). Each worker writes the file at most once.

Workers can stall at any point for an unbounded time (garbage-collection pauses, VM migration,
slow network), and they learn nothing about lease expiry while stalled: a worker that has acquired
the lock keeps believing it holds it.

Writing. Right before writing, the worker asks the lock service whether it still holds an unexpired
lease, and writes only if the answer is yes; if the lease has expired it abandons the job. The
storage service accepts any write; the token is logged for auditing only.

Initially the lock is free, no token has been issued yet (the counter is at k0), the storage has seen token k0, and neither worker has acquired the lock.

Product page cache (design doc)

Product details live in a database and are cached in a key-value cache using the cache-aside

**Yes, the design can leave the cache stale.**

The design deletes the cache entry and then writes the database, and the reader always stores what it read (plain-set). A reader that read v0 before the writer started can stay delayed through the whole batch. Each delete finds an empty cache, so it removes nothing. After the writer finishes, the reader stores v0 into the empty cache, while the database holds v3. There is no expiry, so the stale entry stays indefinitely. The last update's delete happens before its database write, so nothing deletes the cache entry after the final write.

Event sequence:
1. The reader misses on an empty cache and reads v0 from the database.
2. The writer starts with delete-first.
3. It deletes the empty cache entry, then writes v1.
4. It deletes the empty cache entry again, then writes v2.
5. It deletes the empty cache entry once more, then writes v3.
6. The writer finishes.
7. The delayed reader stores v0 into the empty cache.
8. The cache holds v0, the database holds v3, and the writer is done, so the state is stale.

--- Design document ---
Checkout payment flow (design doc)

When a customer places order o1, the checkout service (the client) sends a charge request to an
external payment provider and waits for the reply. The network between them is unreliable: a request
or a response can be lost, and messages can be delayed arbitrarily, so a request may still be in
transit after the client has stopped waiting for it. The provider serves requests concurrently on
several worker threads, in whatever order they arrive, so the steps of different requests (looking up
records, charging, writing records) can interleave.

Each request is one attempt (a0 for the first try). After sending an attempt the client starts a
timer at t0; every clock tick advances it by one, and when it reaches t11 (11 ticks after sending)
without a response the client gives up on that attempt and retries with the next attempt number
(a1, then a2). At most two retries are made. If a success response arrives while the client is still
waiting, the order is confirmed and no further attempts are made.

Charging and duplicate protection. Every attempt for an order carries the same idempotency key
(derived from the order number). When a request arrives, the provider looks the key up and, in the
same atomic database operation, inserts a reservation if it is absent (an insert-if-absent with a
unique constraint). Only a request whose insert succeeded is approved and charged; when the charge
succeeds the reservation is completed with the stored response. A request whose key already has a
completed record gets the stored success response back without a new charge; a request that finds
only an unfinished reservation is not charged either.

Initially the client is about to send attempt a0 for order o1; nothing has been charged and the provider has no record for o1.

is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
    (dedup-atomic)   ; the provider looks up and reserves the idempotency key in one atomic step
    (dedup-racy)     ; the provider looks up the key, but only records it after the charge succeeds
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-attempt ?a ?b - attempt)   ; attempt ?b is the retry that follows attempt ?a
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick)         ; timer value ?u follows ?t
    (first-tick ?t - tick)           ; timer value right after a request is sent
    (timeout-tick ?t - tick)         ; timer value at which the client gives up waiting
    ;; --- client ---

    (waiting ?o - order ?a - attempt)  ; client sent attempt ?a and awaits the response

    (confirmed ?o - order)             ; client received a success response
    ;; --- network ---
```

Checkout payment flow (design doc)

When a customer places order o1, the checkout service (the client) sends a charge request to an
external payment provider and waits for the reply. The network between them is unreliable: a request
or a response can be lost, and messages can be delayed arbitrarily, so a request may still be in
transit after the client has stopped waiting for it. The provider serves requests concurrently on
several worker threads, in whatever order they arrive, so the steps of different requests (looking up
records, charging, writing records) can interleave.

Each request is one attempt (a0 for the first try). After sending an attempt the client starts a
timer at t0; every clock tick advances it by one, and when it reaches t5 (5 ticks after sending)
without a response the client gives up on that attempt and retries with the next attempt number
(a1, then a2). At most two retries are made. If a success response arrives while the client is still
waiting, the order is confirmed and no further attempts are made.

Charging. The provider treats every request it receives as a new payment: it approves the request
and charges the customer's card, then sends a success response. Requests carry the order number for
bookkeeping only; the provider does not use it to detect repeats.

automatically, after which it continues receiving messages.

table in the payments database. The payout ledger entry and the id record are written in the same

**Verdict: safe under the modelled design, with one caveat about what the model abstracts away.**

The design has a durable dedup table. The ledger entry and the id record are written in one transaction, and the consumer checks the table before paying. That matches the `mode-2` actions: `process-3` marks `processed` and `seen` in a single step, and nothing in `mode-2` ever clears `seen`. `crash-1`, which clears `seen`, requires `mode-1`, which is the in-memory dedup case and not this design.

To get `processed-twice m1`, the only action is `process-again`. It needs `(working w1 m1)`, `(processed m1)` and `(not-seen m1)`.

1. `receive` is the only way to get `working w1 m1`. It needs m1 visible and w1 idle.
2. In `mode-2`, the only way to get `processed m1` is `process-3`, and it sets `seen m1` while removing `not-seen m1`.
3. No `mode-2` action restores `not-seen m1`. `crash-restart` only moves `handled` to `idle`.
4. So whenever `processed m1` holds, `seen m1` holds and `not-seen m1` does not. `process-again` can never fire.

The redelivery scenario fails to violate the requirement:
- w1 receives m1 and processes it, so the payout is made and the id is recorded.
- w1 crashes before acking, or the visibility timeout expires (`reappear`).
- m1 is redelivered, but `seen m1` holds, so only `skip-duplicate` is enabled, followed by `ack`.

**Caveat:** the model treats "bank call + id record" as one atomic step. In the prose, the bank call is outside the DB transaction. A crash after the bank call but before the commit would leave no id record, and the redelivery would pay again. That is a real gap in the design, but it is outside this event model, where no such interleaving exists. To close it, send an idempotency key (the message id) to the bank API.

transit after the client has stopped waiting for it. The provider handles requests one at a time,
in whatever order they arrive.

Each request is one attempt (a0 for the first try). After sending an attempt the client starts a
timer at t0; every clock tick advances it by one, and when it reaches t1 (1 tick after sending)
without a response the client gives up on that attempt and retries with the next attempt number
(a1, then a2). At most two retries are made. If a success response arrives while the client is still
waiting, the order is confirmed and no further attempts are made.

and charges the customer's card, then sends a success response. Requests carry the order number for

Report-generation job: leader lock design (design doc)

Two worker processes, c1 and c2, may both try to run the nightly job, which overwrites a shared file
in object storage. To make sure only one of them writes, a worker must first acquire a lock from the
lock service. The lock is a lease: it is granted for 3 clock ticks, after which the lock service
considers it expired and may grant it to the other worker. Each grant comes with a token from a
counter (k1 for the first grant, then k2, ...; k0 is the initial counter value and is never handed
out). Each worker writes the file at most once.

Workers can stall at any point for an unbounded time (garbage-collection pauses, VM migration,
slow network), and they learn nothing about lease expiry while stalled: a worker that has acquired
the lock keeps believing it holds it.

Writing. Right before writing, the worker asks the lock service whether it still holds an unexpired
lease, and writes only if the answer is yes; if the lease has expired it abandons the job. The
storage service accepts any write; the token is logged for auditing only.

Initially the lock is free, no token has been issued yet (the counter is at k0), the storage has seen token k0, and neither worker has acquired the lock.

completion.text:
**Yes, this can happen.** The lease check and the write are separate steps, and the worker can stall between them (a time-of-check-to-time-of-use race).

The design facts that apply here are `checks-lease` and `no-fencing`. The storage service accepts every write, and the token is only logged.

**Event sequence:**

1. c1 acquires the lock and gets token k1, with lease age t0.
2. c1 does its pre-write lease check. The check passes because c1 is still the holder, so c1 is now "about to write".
3. c1 stalls, for example in a GC pause or VM migration.
4. The lease ages from t0 to t5 over five ticks, and the lock service expires c1's lease and frees the lock.
5. c2 acquires the lock and gets token k2.
6. c2 passes its own lease check and writes the file. Storage applies it with token k2.
7. c1 wakes up. It already passed its check and has no way to learn the lease expired, so it writes. Storage has no fencing, so it accepts the write even though k1 < k2. An expired holder's write is applied after the newer holder's write, which means `corrupted` holds.

**Why the design fails:** the lease check only proves the lease was valid at the moment of the check. It says nothing about the moment of the write, and the stall can fall in between. The only protection that holds across that gap is on the storage side: reject writes whose token is older than the newest token seen (fencing).

**Precondition check on each step:**
- `acquire c1`: c1 is idle, the lock is free, last-issued is k0, and the next token after k0 is k1.
- `check-lease-and-prepare-write c1`: c1 believes it holds the lock and is the holder.
- The five `tick` events move the lease age from t0 to t5.
- `expire c1 t5`: c1 is the holder and t5 is the lease limit.
- `acquire c2`: the lock is free again and last-issued is k1.
- `check-lease-and-prepare-write c2`: c2 believes it holds the lock and is the holder.
- `write-unfenced c2 k2`: no-fencing holds and c2 has may-write, which records `wrote k2`.
- `write-unfenced-over-newer c1 k1 k2`: c1 still has may-write, `wrote k2` holds, and k1 < k2.

```json
"(tick t3 t4)",
```

--- Design document ---
Payout worker: queue consumer design (design doc)

When a seller's balance is settled, a "send payout" message (m1) is put on a message queue. A
consumer process (w1) receives messages from the queue and, for each one, performs the payout by
calling the bank API (an external side effect that cannot be undone), then acknowledges the message
so the queue deletes it.

The queue guarantees at-least-once delivery. A received message is hidden from consumers; if it is
not acknowledged within 5 clock ticks of being received (the visibility timeout) it becomes visible
again and will be delivered again. The consumer process can crash at any moment and is restarted
automatically, after which it continues receiving messages.

Processing. The consumer performs the payout for every message it receives, then acknowledges it.

Initially m1 is in the queue and visible, nothing has been paid out, and w1 is idle.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
(define (domain queue)
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types message consumer tick)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts: exactly one deduplication mode holds ---
    (dedup-none)      ; the consumer processes every delivery
    (dedup-durable)   ; processed ids are recorded in the database, atomically with the side effect
    (dedup-memory)    ; processed ids are recorded in an in-memory set of the consumer process
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick) (zero-tick ?t - tick)
    (visibility-timeout ?t - tick)        ; age at which an unacknowledged message becomes visible again
    ;; --- queue ---
    (in-queue ?m - message) (visible ?m - message) (hidden ?m - message ?t - tick) (acked ?m - message)
    ;; --- consumer ---
    (idle ?w - consumer) (working ?w - consumer ?m - message) (handled ?w - consumer ?m - message)
    ;; --- effects of processing ---
    (unprocessed ?m - message) (processed ?m - message) (processed-twice ?m - message)
    (not-seen ?m - message) (seen ?m - message))

  (:action receive
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (idle ?w) (visible ?m) (in-queue ?m) (zero-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (idle ?w)) (not (visible ?m)) (working ?w ?m) (hidden ?m ?t)))
  (:action process-without-dedup
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (dedup-none) (working ?w ?m) (unprocessed ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (not (unprocessed ?m)) (processed ?m) (handled ?w ?m)))
  (:action process-and-record-durably
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (dedup-durable) (working ?w ?m) (unprocessed ?m) (not-seen ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (not (unprocessed ?m)) (not (not-seen ?m)) (seen ?m)

  (:action process-and-record-in-memory
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (dedup-memory) (working ?w ?m) (unprocessed ?m) (not-seen ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (not (unprocessed ?m)) (not (not-seen ?m)) (seen ?m)
                 (processed ?m) (handled ?w ?m)))
  (:action skip-duplicate
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (working ?w ?m) (seen ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (handled ?w ?m)))
  (:action process-again
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (working ?w ?m) (processed ?m) (not-seen ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (processed-twice ?m) (handled ?w ?m)))
  (:action ack
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (handled ?w ?m) (hidden ?m ?t))
    :effect (and (not (handled ?w ?m)) (not (hidden ?m ?t)) (not (in-queue ?m)) (idle ?w) (acked ?m)))
  (:action tick

    :effect (and (not (hidden ?m ?t)) (hidden ?m ?u)))

    :precondition (and (hidden ?m ?t) (visibility-timeout ?t) (in-queue ?m))
    :effect (and (not (hidden ?m ?t)) (visible ?m)))
  (:action crash-restart

    :precondition (handled ?w ?m)
    :effect (and (not (handled ?w ?m)) (idle ?w)))
  (:action crash-restart-losing-memory

    :precondition (and (dedup-memory) (handled ?w ?m) (seen ?m))
```

Question: Can the payout for message m1 be performed twice? In the event model this means reaching a state where (processed-twice m1) holds.

If it can happen, give a complete event sequence, starting from the initial situation described in
the design document, that ends in such a state: a list of ground actions such as "(action arg1 arg2)".

completion.text:
**Yes, the payout can be performed twice.** The design uses no deduplication (`dedup-none`), so the consumer pays out on every delivery. The queue is at-least-once, so a crash between the payout and the ack lets the message reappear and be paid again.

**How it happens:**
1. w1 receives m1, which is now hidden at age t0.
2. w1 performs the bank payout, so m1 is processed once, and w1 is now holding the message to ack.
3. w1 crashes before acking and restarts idle. m1 is still in the queue, hidden and unacknowledged.
4. Five ticks pass, taking m1 from age t0 to t5, which is the visibility timeout. m1 becomes visible again.
5. The restarted w1 receives m1 a second time.
6. Nothing records that m1 was already paid and `not-seen` still holds, so w1 pays again (`process-again`) and `processed-twice m1` holds.

Each step's precondition holds:
- `receive`: w1 is idle, m1 is visible and in the queue, and t0 is the zero tick.
- `process-without-dedup`: `dedup-none` holds, w1 is working on m1, and m1 is unprocessed.
- `crash-restart`: `handled w1 m1` holds after the payout.
- `tick` and `reappear`: m1 is hidden at the right age, and t5 is the visibility timeout.
- `process-again`: w1 is working on m1, m1 is processed, and `not-seen` holds because `dedup-none` never sets `seen`.

```json
"(tick m1 t0 t1)",
"(tick m1 t1 t2)",
"(tick m1 t2 t3)",
"(tick m1 t3 t4)",
"(tick m1 t4 t5)",
"(reappear m1 t5)",
"(receive w1 m1 t0)",
"(process-again w1 m1)"
```

purchase.

back into stock so that another customer can buy it. Customers can be slow to pay; the payment step
may happen at any later time.

above zero, and then, as a separate statement, writes back the count it read minus one. No lock or
transaction spans the read and the write.

for an expired hold is refused and the customer must start again.

**Verdict: violation.** The dedup set lives only in the consumer's process memory, so a crash wipes it. That corresponds to the `mode-1` design in the model, where `crash-1` clears `seen`.

**Event sequence**

1. `receive`: w1 takes m1, which becomes hidden at age t0.
2. `process-1`: w1 credits the wallet and records m1 in its in-memory set (`processed`, `seen`). The credit is committed, but w1 has not yet acknowledged.
3. Five `tick` events advance m1's age from t0 to t5, which is the visibility timeout.
4. `reappear`: m1 is still in the queue because it was never acked, so it becomes visible again.
5. `crash-1`: w1 crashes and restarts. Its in-memory set is lost (`seen` is cleared, `not-seen` holds) and w1 is idle again.
6. `receive`: w1 gets m1 a second time.
7. `process-again`: the set no longer contains m1, so w1 credits the wallet a second time. This gives `processed-twice m1`.

The crash can happen after the credit but before the ack, and the ack never arrives within the 5-tick window. At-least-once redelivery then combines with the lost dedup state to cause a double payout. Making the dedup record durable and atomic with the credit (for example, a unique payout-id constraint in the payments DB, written in the same transaction as the credit) would close this hole.

--- Design document ---
Checkout payment flow (design doc)

When a customer places order o1, the checkout service (the client) sends a charge request to an
external payment provider and waits for the reply. The network between them is unreliable: a request
or a response can be lost, and messages can be delayed arbitrarily, so a request may still be in
transit after the client has stopped waiting for it. The provider handles requests one at a time,
in whatever order they arrive.

Each request is one attempt (a0 for the first try). After sending an attempt the client starts a
timer at t0; every clock tick advances it by one, and when it reaches t7 (7 ticks after sending)
without a response the client gives up on that attempt and retries with the next attempt number
(a1, then a2). At most two retries are made. If a success response arrives while the client is still
waiting, the order is confirmed and no further attempts are made.

Charging and duplicate protection. Every attempt for an order carries the same idempotency key
(derived from the order number). When a request arrives, the provider looks the key up and, in the
same atomic database operation, inserts a reservation if it is absent (an insert-if-absent with a
unique constraint). Only a request whose insert succeeded is approved and charged; when the charge
succeeds the reservation is completed with the stored response. A request whose key already has a
completed record gets the stored success response back without a new charge; a request that finds
only an unfinished reservation is not charged either.

Initially the client is about to send attempt a0 for order o1; nothing has been charged and the provider has no record for o1.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl

  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types order attempt tick)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts (which of these hold depends on the design) ---
    (mode-1)
    (mode-3)
    (mode-2)
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-attempt ?a ?b - attempt)   ; attempt ?b is the retry that follows attempt ?a
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick)         ; timer value ?u follows ?t
    (first-tick ?t - tick)           ; timer value right after a request is sent
    (timeout-tick ?t - tick)         ; timer value at which the client gives up waiting
    ;; --- client ---
    (ready ?o - order ?a - attempt)    ; client is about to send attempt ?a for order ?o
    (waiting ?o - order ?a - attempt)  ; client sent attempt ?a and awaits the response
    (clock ?o - order ?t - tick)       ; client's timer for the outstanding attempt
    (confirmed ?o - order)             ; client received a success response
    ;; --- network ---
    (in-flight ?o - order ?a - attempt) ; request of attempt ?a travelling to the provider
    (response ?o - order)               ; success response travelling back to the client
    ;; --- provider ---
    (approved ?o - order ?a - attempt)  ; provider accepted attempt ?a and will charge it
    (no-record ?o - order)              ; no idempotency record (and no reservation) for ?o yet
    (record ?o - order)                 ; idempotency record for ?o stored
    (uncharged ?o - order)

    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action accept-1

    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (approved ?o ?a)))

    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (response ?o)))

    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (response ?o)))

  (:action charge-again

    :precondition (and (approved ?o ?a) (charged ?o))

  (:action lose-response

  (:action receive-response
```

completion.text:
**Verdict: safe.** The design cannot charge o1 twice.

The model's three modes are variants of the provider's duplicate check. The design describes an atomic insert-if-absent on a unique key, where only the request whose insert succeeds is approved. That matches `mode-3`, where `accept-1` and `replay-2` are the enabled actions. The other two modes would model weaker designs: `mode-1` has no check at all, and `mode-2` has a non-atomic check that only clears the record at charge time.

**Why `(charged-twice o1)` is unreachable under `mode-3`:**

1. `charged-twice` is only produced by `charge-again`. That action needs `(approved o1 ?a)` while `(charged o1)` already holds, so it needs a second approval after the first charge.
2. In `mode-3`, the only action that produces `approved` is `accept-1`. It requires `(no-record o1)` and deletes it in the same step, which models the atomic reservation.
3. Nothing ever re-adds `no-record`. `charge` only deletes it, and `lose-request`, the client actions and the tick actions don't touch it. So `accept-1` can fire at most once, and at most one `approved` fact is ever created for o1.
4. That single approval can be consumed by only one of two actions:
   - `charge`, which needs `uncharged`. It sets `charged`, and then no approval is left for `charge-again`.
   - `charge-again`, which needs `charged`. It cannot fire first, because `charged` is only set by `charge`.
5. The other provider actions don't create approvals. Later attempts that arrive find `no-record` false. If the charge has already completed, `record` is true and they fire `replay-2`, which only sends a response. If the charge hasn't completed yet, neither fires, so the request stays unprocessed (it can still be lost). Neither case charges anything.

Timeout-and-retry races, such as a late a0 arriving after a1 or a2 was sent, only create extra in-flight requests. Those requests are replays or no-ops, never approvals. There is no event sequence reaching the violation.


prompt:
--- Design document ---
Report-generation job: leader lock design (design doc)

Two worker processes, c1 and c2, may both try to run the nightly job, which overwrites a shared file
in object storage. To make sure only one of them writes, a worker must first acquire a lock from the
lock service. The lock is a lease: it is granted for 7 clock ticks, after which the lock service
considers it expired and may grant it to the other worker. Each grant comes with a token from a
counter (k1 for the first grant, then k2, ...; k0 is the initial counter value and is never handed
out). Each worker writes the file at most once.

Workers can stall at any point for an unbounded time (garbage-collection pauses, VM migration,
slow network), and they learn nothing about lease expiry while stalled: a worker that has acquired
the lock keeps believing it holds it.

Writing. Right before writing, the worker asks the lock service whether it still holds an unexpired
lease, and writes only if the answer is yes; if the lease has expired it abandons the job. The
storage service accepts any write; the token is logged for auditing only.

Initially the lock is free, no token has been issued yet (the counter is at k0), the storage has seen token k0, and neither worker has acquired the lock.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl

  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types client tick token)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts (which of these hold depends on the design) ---
    (mode-3)
    (mode-2)
    (mode-1)
    (mode-4)
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick) (zero-tick ?t - tick)
    (lease-limit ?t - tick)              ; lease age at which the lock service expires the lease
    (next-token ?k ?l - token)           ; token ?l is issued after ?k
    (token-less ?k ?l - token)           ; ?k < ?l
    (token-leq ?k ?l - token)            ; ?k <= ?l
    ;; --- lock service ---
    (lock-free) (holder ?c - client) (lease-age ?t - tick) (last-issued ?k - token)
    ;; --- clients ---
    (idle ?c - client)                   ; has not acquired the lock yet
    (believes ?c - client)               ; client thinks it holds the lock
    (lease-expired ?c - client)          ; the service expired this client's lease
    (token-of ?c - client ?k - token)
    (may-write ?c - client)              ; client is about to write to storage
    ;; --- storage ---
    (max-seen ?k - token)                ; newest token storage has seen (used with mode-3)
    (wrote ?k - token)                   ; a write with token ?k was applied
    (corrupted))                         ; an older holder's write was applied after a newer holder's write

  (:action acquire
    :parameters (?c - client ?k ?l - token ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (idle ?c) (lock-free) (last-issued ?k) (next-token ?k ?l) (zero-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (idle ?c)) (not (lock-free)) (not (last-issued ?k)) (last-issued ?l)
                 (holder ?c) (believes ?c) (token-of ?c ?l) (lease-age ?t)))
  (:action tick
    :parameters (?t ?u - tick)
    :precondition (and (lease-age ?t) (next-tick ?t ?u))
    :effect (and (not (lease-age ?t)) (lease-age ?u)))
  (:action expire

    :precondition (and (holder ?c) (lease-age ?t) (lease-limit ?t))
    :effect (and (not (holder ?c)) (not (lease-age ?t)) (lock-free) (lease-expired ?c)))
  (:action prepare-1
    :parameters (?c - client)
    :precondition (and (mode-4) (believes ?c))
    :effect (may-write ?c))
  (:action check-1
    :parameters (?c - client)
    :precondition (and (mode-1) (believes ?c) (holder ?c))
    :effect (may-write ?c))

    :precondition (and (mode-2) (may-write ?c) (token-of ?c ?k))
    :effect (and (not (may-write ?c)) (not (believes ?c)) (wrote ?k)))

    :effect (and (not (may-write ?c)) (not (believes ?c)) (not (max-seen ?j)) (max-seen ?k) (wrote ?k)))
  (:action write-2
```

completion.text:
**Which modes hold.** The design says the worker asks the lock service right before writing and writes only if the lease is unexpired. That is `check-1`, so `mode-1` holds. The storage service accepts any write and logs the token only. That is `write-4`/`write-1`, so `mode-2` holds. **Other paths to stale.** `fill-2` also requires `cache-empty`, so the cache never holds two versions. Every path to `(cache v)` with `v` older than `db w` after `writer-done` requires a fill of an old value after the last invalidate, and the lease check blocks that.

No event sequence reaches `(stale)`, so the design is safe.

idempotency table. If a record is found, the provider does not charge again; it just returns the

```python
def can_split_evenly(xs):
    """Return True if the values in `xs` can be divided into two groups with equal sums,
    each value going to exactly one of the groups (a group may be empty), and False
    otherwise.
    """
    total = sum(xs)
    if total % 2 == 1:
        return False
    target = total // 2
    reachable = [True] + [False] * target
    for x in xs:
        for s in range(target, x - 2, -1):
            if reachable[s - x]:
                reachable[s] = True
    return reachable[target]
```

I found no valid input where the function misbehaves.

**The loop bound.** The inner loop is `range(target, x - 2, -1)`. A standard subset-sum loop would stop at `x`, so it would be `range(target, x - 1, -1)`. This version runs one step further, to `s = x - 1`. At that step, `s - x = -1`, so `reachable[-1]` is read. In Python that is the last element, `reachable[target]`.

**Effect of the extra step.** When `reachable[target]` is `True`, the extra step sets `reachable[x-1] = True`. That value may be spurious. But `reachable[target]` is already `True`, and entries only ever change from `False` to `True`. So the final return value is `True` either way, and the spurious entry can't change it. If `reachable[target]` is `False`, the extra step does nothing.

**Edge cases.**
- **`x = 0`:** The extra step is `s = -1`, which sets `reachable[-1]` from itself. That changes nothing.
- **`x - 1 == target`:** The step sets `reachable[target]` from `reachable[-1]`, which is the same cell. That changes nothing.
- **`x - 2 >= target`:** The range is empty, so there is no index error.
- **Empty list:** The total is 0 and the target is 0. `reachable = [True]` and the function returns `True`, which is correct because both groups are empty and sum to 0.
- **Odd total:** The function returns `False`, which is correct.
- **Indexing:** `s` is never below -1 and `s - x` is never below -1, so there are no out-of-range accesses.

Checkout payment flow (design doc)

When a customer places order o1, the checkout service (the client) sends a charge request to an
external payment provider and waits for the reply. The network between them is unreliable: a request
or a response can be lost, and messages can be delayed arbitrarily, so a request may still be in
transit after the client has stopped waiting for it. The provider handles requests one at a time,
in whatever order they arrive.

Each request is one attempt (a0 for the first try). After sending an attempt the client starts a
timer at t0; every clock tick advances it by one, and when it reaches t5 (5 ticks after sending)
without a response the client gives up on that attempt and retries with the next attempt number
(a1, then a2). At most two retries are made. If a success response arrives while the client is still
waiting, the order is confirmed and no further attempts are made.

(derived from the order number). When a request arrives, the provider looks the key up and, in the
same atomic database operation, inserts a reservation if it is absent (an insert-if-absent with a
unique constraint). Only a request whose insert succeeded is approved and charged; when the charge
succeeds the reservation is completed with the stored response. A request whose key already has a
completed record gets the stored success response back without a new charge; a request that finds

**Verdict: safe.** Under this design the card cannot be charged twice for o1.

**Which model actions apply.** The design says the provider looks up the idempotency key and inserts a reservation in one atomic insert-if-absent, and that only the request whose insert succeeded is approved. In the model this is `accept-1`, which is guarded by `mode-3`. It requires `(no-record o1)` and deletes it in the same step as it adds `(approved o1 a)`. The other accept actions (`accept-2`, `accept-3`) belong to the other designs: no dedup check at all, or a check that does not consume the reservation. They are not enabled here.

**Why `charged-twice` is unreachable.**
1. `charged-twice` is produced only by `charge-again`, which needs `(approved o1 a)` for some attempt while `(charged o1)` already holds.
2. `approved` is added only by `accept-1`, which needs `(no-record o1)`.
3. `no-record o1` is true initially and is never added back by any action. `accept-1` and `charge` only delete it. So `accept-1` can fire at most once, and at most one `approved o1 _` fact ever exists.
4. That single approval is consumed by `charge` (since `uncharged o1` holds initially) or, if `charge-again` were possible, by that. `charge-again` needs `charged o1`, and `charged o1` is only set by the `charge` that consumes the one approval. After that no approval remains, so `charge-again` can never fire.
5. Any later duplicate request hits one of two cases:
   - If the reservation exists but the charge has not finished, no `accept-1` or `replay-2` is enabled (`no-record` is false and `record` is not yet true). The request just sits in flight or is lost, and is never charged.
   - If the record exists, `replay-2` returns the stored response without a charge.

**Interleavings checked.** Request loss, response loss, delayed requests arriving after a timeout, and retries a1 and a2 can all change what the client sees. They can leave the client unconfirmed, but none of them creates a second approval. Duplicates therefore never reach `charge-again`.

--- Design document ---
Report-generation job: leader lock design (design doc)

Two worker processes, c1 and c2, may both try to run the nightly job, which overwrites a shared file
in object storage. To make sure only one of them writes, a worker must first acquire a lock from the
lock service. The lock is a lease: it is granted for 7 clock ticks, after which the lock service
considers it expired and may grant it to the other worker. Each grant comes with a token from a
counter (k1 for the first grant, then k2, ...; k0 is the initial counter value and is never handed
out). Each worker writes the file at most once.

Workers can stall at any point for an unbounded time (garbage-collection pauses, VM migration,
slow network), and they learn nothing about lease expiry while stalled: a worker that has acquired
the lock keeps believing it holds it.

Writing. Right before writing, the worker asks the lock service whether it still holds an unexpired
lease, and writes only if the answer is yes; if the lease has expired it abandons the job. The
storage service accepts any write; the token is logged for auditing only.

--- Design document ---
Limited-edition drop: stock reservation design (design doc)

The shop has 1 unit of a limited-edition item in stock, and 2 customers (c1, c2) try to buy
it at the same time. Each customer's checkout runs on its own server thread; the threads interleave
arbitrarily. A checkout first reserves a unit (a hold), then the customer pays to confirm the
purchase.

Holds are temporary: a hold that is not paid for expires after 1 clock tick, and the unit goes
back into stock so that another customer can buy it. Customers can be slow to pay; the payment step
may happen at any later time.

Reserving. The checkout thread reserves with a single atomic conditional update
(UPDATE stock SET count = count - 1 WHERE count > 0); if no row is updated the customer is told the
item is sold out.

Paying. The payment service confirms an order only if the customer's hold is still active; payment
for an expired hold is refused and the customer must start again.

Initially all customers are browsing and the stock count is 1.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types customer level tick)
  (:predicates

    (stock-atomic)      ; checkout decrements stock with one atomic conditional update
    (pay-checks-hold)   ; payment is accepted only while the customer's hold is still active
    (pay-ignores-hold)  ; payment is accepted even after the hold has expired
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-level ?lower ?higher - level)  ; stock level ?higher is one more than ?lower
    (zero-tick ?t - tick)
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick)
    (hold-limit ?t - tick)               ; hold age at which a hold expires

    (stock ?q - level)                   ; current stock level

    (read-stock ?c - customer ?q - level) ; (racy) checkout of ?c read stock level ?q
    (holding ?c - customer)              ; customer holds one reserved unit
    (hold-age ?c - customer ?t - tick)
    (expired ?c - customer)              ; customer's hold expired and its unit went back to stock
    (sold ?c - customer))                ; customer's purchase is confirmed

    :parameters (?c - customer ?q ?p - level)
    :precondition (and (stock-racy) (browsing ?c) (stock ?q) (next-level ?p ?q))
```

```python
def is_monotone(xs):
    """Return True if `xs` is entirely non-decreasing or entirely non-increasing (lists
    with fewer than two elements count as both), and False otherwise.
    """
    inc = True
    dec = True
    for i in range(1, len(xs)):
        if xs[i] < xs[i - 1]:
            inc = False
        if xs[i] > xs[i - 1]:
            dec = False
    return inc or dec
```

--- Design document ---
Report-generation job: leader lock design (design doc)

Two worker processes, c1 and c2, may both try to run the nightly job, which overwrites a shared file
in object storage. To make sure only one of them writes, a worker must first acquire a lock from the
lock service. The lock is a lease: it is granted for 3 clock ticks, after which the lock service
considers it expired and may grant it to the other worker. Each grant comes with a token from a
counter (k1 for the first grant, then k2, ...; k0 is the initial counter value and is never handed
out). Each worker writes the file at most once.

Workers can stall at any point for an unbounded time (garbage-collection pauses, VM migration,
slow network), and they learn nothing about lease expiry while stalled: a worker that has acquired
the lock keeps believing it holds it.

Writing. Once a worker holds the lock it writes the file. The storage service accepts any write;
the token is logged for auditing only.

Initially the lock is free, no token has been issued yet (the counter is at k0), the storage has seen token k0, and neither worker has acquired the lock.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
(define (domain lease-lock)
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types client tick token)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts ---
    (fencing)          ; storage rejects writes whose token is older than the newest it has seen
    (no-fencing)       ; storage accepts every write
    (checks-lease)     ; a client checks it still holds the lease right before writing
    (no-lease-check)   ; a client writes whenever it believes it holds the lock
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick) (zero-tick ?t - tick)
    (lease-limit ?t - tick)              ; lease age at which the lock service expires the lease
    (next-token ?k ?l - token)           ; token ?l is issued after ?k
    (token-less ?k ?l - token)           ; ?k < ?l
    (token-leq ?k ?l - token)            ; ?k <= ?l
    ;; --- lock service ---
    (lock-free) (holder ?c - client) (lease-age ?t - tick) (last-issued ?k - token)
    ;; --- clients ---
    (idle ?c - client)                   ; has not acquired the lock yet
    (believes ?c - client)               ; client thinks it holds the lock
    (lease-expired ?c - client)          ; the service expired this client's lease
    (token-of ?c - client ?k - token)
    (may-write ?c - client)              ; client is about to write to storage
    ;; --- storage ---
    (max-seen ?k - token)                ; newest token storage has seen (used with fencing)
    (wrote ?k - token)                   ; a write with token ?k was applied
    (corrupted))                         ; an older holder's write was applied after a newer holder's write

  (:action acquire
    :parameters (?c - client ?k ?l - token ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (idle ?c) (lock-free) (last-issued ?k) (next-token ?k ?l) (zero-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (idle ?c)) (not (lock-free)) (not (last-issued ?k)) (last-issued ?l)
                 (holder ?c) (believes ?c) (token-of ?c ?l) (lease-age ?t)))
  (:action tick
    :parameters (?t ?u - tick)
    :precondition (and (lease-age ?t) (next-tick ?t ?u))
    :effect (and (not (lease-age ?t)) (lease-age ?u)))
  (:action expire
    :parameters (?c - client ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (holder ?c) (lease-age ?t) (lease-limit ?t))
    :effect (and (not (holder ?c)) (not (lease-age ?t)) (lock-free) (lease-expired ?c)))
  (:action prepare-write
    :parameters (?c - client)
    :precondition (and (no-lease-check) (believes ?c))
    :effect (may-write ?c))
  (:action check-lease-and-prepare-write
    :parameters (?c - client)
    :precondition (and (checks-lease) (believes ?c) (holder ?c))
    :effect (may-write ?c))
  (:action write-unfenced
    :parameters (?c - client ?k - token)
    :precondition (and (no-fencing) (may-write ?c) (token-of ?c ?k))
    :effect (and (not (may-write ?c)) (not (believes ?c)) (wrote ?k)))
  (:action write-unfenced-over-newer
    :parameters (?c - client ?k ?m - token)
    :precondition (and (no-fencing) (may-write ?c) (token-of ?c ?k) (wrote ?m) (token-less ?k ?m))
    :effect (and (not (may-write ?c)) (not (believes ?c)) (corrupted)))
  (:action write-fenced
    :parameters (?c - client ?k ?j - token)
    :precondition (and (fencing) (may-write ?c) (token-of ?c ?k) (max-seen ?j) (token-leq ?j ?k))
    :effect (and (not (may-write ?c)) (not (believes ?c)) (not (max-seen ?j)) (max-seen ?k) (wrote ?k)))
  (:action write-fenced-over-newer
    :parameters (?c - client ?k ?j ?m - token)
    :precondition (and (fencing) (may-write ?c) (token-of ?c ?k) (max-seen ?j) (token-leq ?j ?k)

    :effect (and (not (may-write ?c)) (not (believes ?c)) (corrupted)))
  (:action reject-stale-write

    :precondition (and (fencing) (may-write ?c) (token-of ?c ?k) (max-seen ?j) (token-less ?k ?j))
    :effect (and (not (may-write ?c)) (not (believes ?c)))))
```

**Yes, this can happen.** The design has no fencing and no lease check, so the storage service accepts a stale write after a newer one.

I read the initial state as `no-fencing` and `no-lease-check` holding, the lock free, the counter at k0, and both clients idle. I take `lease-limit` to be t3, matching the 3-tick lease.

**Event sequence:**
1. c1 acquires the lock and gets token k1, with lease age t0.
2. c1 stalls. It still has `believes c1`, because it learns nothing about expiry.
3. The lease ticks t0→t1→t2→t3.
4. The lock service expires c1's lease at age t3. The lock becomes free and `lease-expired c1` is set, but `believes c1` stays true.
5. c2 acquires the lock and gets token k2, since the last issued token is k1.
6. c2 prepares its write. `no-lease-check` holds and c2 believes it holds the lock.
7. c2 writes without fencing, so `wrote k2` becomes true.
8. c1 wakes up and prepares its write. `no-lease-check` holds and `believes c1` is still true, so no lease check stops it.
9. c1 writes with token k1. Because `wrote k2` holds and k1 < k2, the write is applied over the newer one, and `corrupted` becomes true.

**Fix:** the storage service should reject writes whose token is older than the newest it has seen (fencing). A lease check by the client alone is not enough, because the worker can still stall between the check and the write.

--- Design document ---
Checkout payment flow (design doc)

When a customer places order o1, the checkout service (the client) sends a charge request to an
external payment provider and waits for the reply. The network between them is unreliable: a request
or a response can be lost, and messages can be delayed arbitrarily, so a request may still be in
transit after the client has stopped waiting for it. The provider handles requests one at a time,
in whatever order they arrive.

Each request is one attempt (a0 for the first try). After sending an attempt the client starts a
timer at t0; every clock tick advances it by one, and when it reaches t5 (5 ticks after sending)
without a response the client gives up on that attempt and retries with the next attempt number
(a1, then a2). At most two retries are made. If a success response arrives while the client is still
waiting, the order is confirmed and no further attempts are made.

Charging and duplicate protection. Every attempt for an order carries the same idempotency key
(derived from the order number). When a request arrives, the provider looks the key up and, in the
same atomic database operation, inserts a reservation if it is absent (an insert-if-absent with a
unique constraint). Only a request whose insert succeeded is approved and charged; when the charge
succeeds the reservation is completed with the stored response. A request whose key already has a
completed record gets the stored success response back without a new charge; a request that finds
only an unfinished reservation is not charged either.

Initially the client is about to send attempt a0 for order o1; nothing has been charged and the provider has no record for o1.

is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types order attempt tick)
  (:predicates

    (dedup-none)     ; the provider does not deduplicate requests
    (dedup-atomic)   ; the provider looks up and reserves the idempotency key in one atomic step
    (dedup-racy)     ; the provider looks up the key, but only records it after the charge succeeds
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-attempt ?a ?b - attempt)   ; attempt ?b is the retry that follows attempt ?a
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick)         ; timer value ?u follows ?t
    (first-tick ?t - tick)           ; timer value right after a request is sent
    (timeout-tick ?t - tick)         ; timer value at which the client gives up waiting
    ;; --- client ---
    (ready ?o - order ?a - attempt)    ; client is about to send attempt ?a for order ?o
    (waiting ?o - order ?a - attempt)  ; client sent attempt ?a and awaits the response
    (clock ?o - order ?t - tick)       ; client's timer for the outstanding attempt
    (confirmed ?o - order)             ; client received a success response

    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (approved ?o ?a)))

    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)

    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (response ?o)))
  (:action charge
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (approved ?o ?a) (uncharged ?o))
    :effect (and (not (approved ?o ?a)) (not (uncharged ?o)) (not (no-record ?o))
                 (charged ?o) (record ?o) (response ?o)))
  (:action charge-again
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (approved ?o ?a) (charged ?o))
    :effect (and (not (approved ?o ?a)) (charged-twice ?o) (response ?o)))
  (:action lose-response
    :parameters (?o - order)

    :effect (not (response ?o)))
  (:action receive-response
```

1. c1 acquires the lock and receives token k1. Its lease age is t0.
2. c1 asks the lock service whether it still holds the lease. The answer is yes, so c1 is about to write (`may-write c1`).
3. c1 stalls (GC pause or VM migration). Meanwhile the lease ages from t0 to t3 over three ticks.
4. The lock service expires c1's lease at t3. The lock is free again.
5. c2 acquires the lock and receives token k2.
6. c2 passes its own lease check.
7. c2 writes with token k2, and storage applies it.
8. c1 wakes up and completes its write using the stale check from step 2. Storage accepts any write, so c1's write with k1 is applied after the write with k2 (k1 < k2). The file is corrupted.

This assumes the lease limit is t3 (a 3-tick lease) and the lock service's last-issued token starts at k0. Both follow from the design document.

prompt:
--- Design document ---
Checkout payment flow (design doc)

When a customer places order o1, the checkout service (the client) sends a charge request to an
external payment provider and waits for the reply. The network between them is unreliable: a request
or a response can be lost, and messages can be delayed arbitrarily, so a request may still be in
transit after the client has stopped waiting for it. The provider handles requests one at a time,
in whatever order they arrive.

Each request is one attempt (a0 for the first try). After sending an attempt the client starts a
timer at t0; every clock tick advances it by one, and when it reaches t5 (5 ticks after sending)
without a response the client gives up on that attempt and retries with the next attempt number
(a1, then a2). At most two retries are made. If a success response arrives while the client is still
waiting, the order is confirmed and no further attempts are made.

Charging and duplicate protection. Every attempt for an order carries the same idempotency key
(derived from the order number). When a request arrives, the provider looks the key up and, in the
same atomic database operation, inserts a reservation if it is absent (an insert-if-absent with a
unique constraint). Only a request whose insert succeeded is approved and charged; when the charge
succeeds the reservation is completed with the stored response. A request whose key already has a
completed record gets the stored success response back without a new charge; a request that finds
only an unfinished reservation is not charged either.

Initially the client is about to send attempt a0 for order o1; nothing has been charged and the provider has no record for o1.

--- Event model ---

is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).
