- 1900 is divisible by 100 but not by 400, so it is not a leap year. The docstring requires 28.

prompt:
--- Design document ---
Report-generation job: leader lock design (design doc)

Two worker processes, c1 and c2, may both try to run the nightly job, which overwrites a shared file
in object storage. To make sure only one of them writes, a worker must first acquire a lock from the
lock service. The lock is a lease: it is granted for 3 clock ticks, after which the lock service
considers it expired and may grant it to the other worker. Each grant comes with a token from a
counter (k1 for the first grant, then k2, ...; k0 is the initial counter value and is never handed
out). Each worker writes the file at most once.

Workers can stall at any point for an unbounded time (garbage-collection pauses, VM migration,
slow network), and they learn nothing about lease expiry while stalled: a worker that has acquired
the lock keeps believing it holds it.

Writing. Right before writing, the worker asks the lock service whether it still holds an unexpired
lease, and writes only if the answer is yes. Every write carries the worker's token, and the storage
service remembers the highest token it has accepted: it rejects any write whose token is lower than
that (fencing), and accepts and records the others.

Initially the lock is free, no token has been issued yet (the counter is at k0), the storage has seen token k0, and neither worker has acquired the lock.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
(define (domain lease-lock)
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types client tick token)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts (which of these hold depends on the design) ---
    (mode-3)
    (mode-2)
    (mode-1)
    (mode-4)
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick) (zero-tick ?t - tick)
    (lease-limit ?t - tick)              ; lease age at which the lock service expires the lease
    (next-token ?k ?l - token)           ; token ?l is issued after ?k
    (token-less ?k ?l - token)           ; ?k < ?l
    (token-leq ?k ?l - token)            ; ?k <= ?l
    ;; --- lock service ---
    (lock-free) (holder ?c - client) (lease-age ?t - tick) (last-issued ?k - token)
    ;; --- clients ---
    (idle ?c - client)                   ; has not acquired the lock yet
    (believes ?c - client)               ; client thinks it holds the lock
    (lease-expired ?c - client)          ; the service expired this client's lease
    (token-of ?c - client ?k - token)
    (may-write ?c - client)              ; client is about to write to storage
    ;; --- storage ---
    (max-seen ?k - token)                ; newest token storage has seen (used with mode-3)
    (wrote ?k - token)                   ; a write with token ?k was applied
    (corrupted))                         ; an older holder's write was applied after a newer holder's write

  (:action acquire
    :parameters (?c - client ?k ?l - token ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (idle ?c) (lock-free) (last-issued ?k) (next-token ?k ?l) (zero-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (idle ?c)) (not (lock-free)) (not (last-issued ?k)) (last-issued ?l)
                 (holder ?c) (believes ?c) (token-of ?c ?l) (lease-age ?t)))
  (:action tick
    :parameters (?t ?u - tick)
    :precondition (and (lease-age ?t) (next-tick ?t ?u))
    :effect (and (not (lease-age ?t)) (lease-age ?u)))
  (:action expire
    :parameters (?c - client ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (holder ?c) (lease-age ?t) (lease-limit ?t))
    :effect (and (not (holder ?c)) (not (lease-age ?t)) (lock-free) (lease-expired ?c)))
  (:action prepare-1
    :parameters (?c - client)
    :precondition (and (mode-4) (believes ?c))
    :effect (may-write ?c))
  (:action check-1
    :parameters (?c - client)
    :precondition (and (mode-1) (believes ?c) (holder ?c))
    :effect (may-write ?c))
  (:action write-4
    :parameters (?c - client ?k - token)
    :precondition (and (mode-2) (may-write ?c) (token-of ?c ?k))
    :effect (and (not (may-write ?c)) (not (believes ?c)) (wrote ?k)))
  (:action write-1
    :parameters (?c - client ?k ?m - token)
    :precondition (and (mode-2) (may-write ?c) (token-of ?c ?k) (wrote ?m) (token-less ?k ?m))
    :effect (and (not (may-write ?c)) (not (believes ?c)) (corrupted)))
  (:action write-3
    :parameters (?c - client ?k ?j - token)
    :precondition (and (mode-3) (may-write ?c) (token-of ?c ?k) (max-seen ?j) (token-leq ?j ?k))
    :effect (and (not (may-write ?c)) (not (believes ?c)) (not (max-seen ?j)) (max-seen ?k) (wrote ?k)))
  (:action write-2
    :parameters (?c - client ?k ?j ?m - token)
    :precondition (and (mode-3) (may-write ?c) (token-of ?c ?k) (max-seen ?j) (token-leq ?j ?k)
                       (wrote ?m) (token-less ?k ?m))
    :effect (and (not (may-write ?c)) (not (believes ?c)) (corrupted)))
  (:action reject-1
    :parameters (?c - client ?k ?j - token)
    :precondition (and (mode-3) (may-write ?c) (token-of ?c ?k) (max-seen ?j) (token-less ?k ?j))
```

Product details live in a database and are cached in a key-value cache using the cache-aside
pattern. One reader process serves product-page requests: on a cache hit it uses the cached value;
on a miss it reads the current value from the database and then stores what it read in the cache.
One writer process applies a batch of 4 price updates to the product, one after another, moving
the database from version v0 to v4. Reader and writer steps interleave arbitrarily, and the reader
can be delayed for any amount of time between reading the database and storing into the cache.
Cache entries have no expiry time.

the product's cache entry. On a miss the reader receives a lease token from the cache; a delete of
the entry revokes any outstanding lease, and the cache only accepts a store from a reader whose
lease is still valid (otherwise the reader drops its value).

Initially the database holds v0, the cache is empty, the reader is idle, and the writer is about to start its first update.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
(define (domain cache-aside)
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types version)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts ---
    (update-then-delete)   ; the writer updates the database, then deletes the cache entry
    (delete-then-update)   ; the writer deletes the cache entry, then updates the database
    (plain-set)            ; a reader that missed always stores the value it read
    (leased-set)           ; a reader may store its value only if its lease was not revoked by a delete
    ;; --- static ---
    (next-version ?v ?w - version) (older ?v ?w - version) (final-version ?v - version)
    ;; --- state ---
    (db ?v - version) (cache ?v - version) (cache-empty)
    (reader-idle) (reader-has ?v - version) (lease)
    (writer-start ?v - version)        ; writer is about to begin its updates (database at ?v)
    (writer-update ?v - version)       ; writer's next step: write the version after ?v to the database
    (writer-invalidate ?v - version)   ; writer's next step: delete the cache entry (database is at ?v)
    (writer-done)
    (stale))                           ; after the writer finished, the cache holds an older version than the database

    :parameters (?v - version)
    :precondition (and (reader-idle) (cache-empty) (db ?v))
    :effect (and (not (reader-idle)) (reader-has ?v) (lease)))

    :parameters (?v - version)
    :precondition (and (plain-set) (reader-has ?v) (cache-empty))
    :effect (and (not (reader-has ?v)) (not (cache-empty)) (cache ?v) (reader-idle)))

    :precondition (and (leased-set) (reader-has ?v) (cache-empty) (lease))

    :effect (and (not (writer-invalidate ?v)) (not (lease)) (writer-update ?v)))

    :precondition (and (delete-then-update) (writer-invalidate ?v) (final-version ?v))
    :effect (and (not (writer-invalidate ?v)) (writer-done)))
```

Question: Can the cache be left holding an older version than the database after the writer has finished all its updates? In the event model this means reaching a state where (stale) holds.

the design document, that ends in such a state: a list of ground actions such as "(action arg1 arg2)".
Every action's precondition must hold at the moment it occurs. If it cannot happen under this design,
say so.

{"verdict": "violation", "trace": ["(action arg ...)", ...]}
or

completion.text:
**Verdict: safe.** The design cannot reach `(stale)`.

**Which design facts hold.** The doc specifies update-then-delete and leased stores, so `update-then-delete` and `leased-set` are true. `delete-then-update` and `plain-set` are false. That disables `begin-delete-first`, `finish-after-update` and `fill-cache`.

**What `(stale)` needs.** `observe-stale` requires `writer-done`, a cache entry `v`, and a database version `w` with `v` older than `w`.
- `writer-done` is only set by `finish-after-delete`. That action needs `writer-update v4`.
- `writer-update v4` is only produced by `invalidate` or `invalidate-empty` on `writer-invalidate v4`, which is the delete that follows the final `write-db`.
- So the last event before `writer-done` is a cache delete, performed after the database reached v4.

**State after that final delete.**
- Both delete actions leave the cache empty and clear `lease`.
- With the lease cleared, a reader holding an old value cannot store it. `fill-cache-with-lease` needs `lease`, and `fill-cache` is disabled. That reader can only `abandon-fill`.
- A new reader must go through `read-miss`, which requires `cache-empty` and reads `db`. The database is v4 and never changes again, so the only value any reader can store is v4.
- The cache therefore holds either nothing or v4, never an older version, so `observe-stale` cannot fire.

**Why the earlier stale-looking windows don't matter.** A reader that reads v_k with a lease and then stores it after a `write-db`, but before the next delete, does leave an older value in the cache. Example: it reads v3, the writer writes v4, and the reader fills v3. That entry is transient. The writer's pending delete of the same version step removes it, because `invalidate` accepts any `cache ?x`. After that delete, no stale value can be re-stored. Every `write-db` is followed by a delete that revokes the lease, so a stale store can happen only before that delete, and the delete then removes it.


completion.text:
**Verdict: violation.** The payout can be performed twice.

The design's mode is "process every delivery", so `dedup-none` holds. Processing a message does not mark it as seen, so `not-seen m1` stays true. I take `not-seen m1` to be true initially. It is a closed-world fact that the document does not state explicitly, and the trace depends on it.

**Event sequence:**
1. `w1` receives m1. It becomes hidden at age t0 and `w1` is working on it.
2. `w1` calls the bank API, so m1 is processed (the first payout). It is now `handled` but not yet acked.
3. `w1` crashes before it acks. The crash-restart returns it to idle. The message is still in the queue and hidden.
4. Eleven ticks pass, taking m1 from t0 to t11. This is the visibility timeout.
5. m1 reappears and becomes visible again, because it was never acknowledged.
6. The restarted `w1` is idle and receives m1 again.
7. With no deduplication, `w1` processes it again. `processed m1` and `not-seen m1` both hold, so `process-again` fires and the payout is performed a second time, giving `processed-twice m1`.

The crash can equally happen after the timeout fires. The ordering in the trace is just one valid one. The cause is the same either way: the bank call and the ack are not atomic, and nothing in the design deduplicates redeliveries.

system: You are a principal engineer running a pre-mortem on a distributed-system design: you look for concrete event sequences that make the system violate its safety requirement. You reason carefully and step by step; you have no tools.
prompt:
--- Design document ---
Checkout payment flow (design doc)

When a customer places order o1, the checkout service (the client) sends a charge request to an
external payment provider and waits for the reply. The network between them is unreliable: a request
or a response can be lost, and messages can be delayed arbitrarily, so a request may still be in
transit after the client has stopped waiting for it. The provider serves requests concurrently on
several worker threads, in whatever order they arrive, so the steps of different requests (looking up
records, charging, writing records) can interleave.

Each request is one attempt (a0 for the first try). After sending an attempt the client starts a
timer at t0; every clock tick advances it by one, and when it reaches t7 (7 ticks after sending)
without a response the client gives up on that attempt and retries with the next attempt number
(a1, then a2). At most two retries are made. If a success response arrives while the client is still
waiting, the order is confirmed and no further attempts are made.

Charging and duplicate protection. Every attempt for an order carries the same idempotency key
(derived from the order number). When a request arrives, the provider looks the key up and, in the
same atomic database operation, inserts a reservation if it is absent (an insert-if-absent with a
unique constraint). Only a request whose insert succeeded is approved and charged; when the charge
succeeds the reservation is completed with the stored response. A request whose key already has a
completed record gets the stored success response back without a new charge; a request that finds
only an unfinished reservation is not charged either.

Initially the client is about to send attempt a0 for order o1; nothing has been charged and the provider has no record for o1.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
(define (domain payments)
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types order attempt tick)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts: exactly one deduplication mode holds ---
    (dedup-none)     ; the provider does not deduplicate requests
    (dedup-atomic)   ; the provider looks up and reserves the idempotency key in one atomic step
    (dedup-racy)     ; the provider looks up the key, but only records it after the charge succeeds
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-attempt ?a ?b - attempt)   ; attempt ?b is the retry that follows attempt ?a
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick)         ; timer value ?u follows ?t
    (first-tick ?t - tick)           ; timer value right after a request is sent
    (timeout-tick ?t - tick)         ; timer value at which the client gives up waiting
    ;; --- client ---
    (ready ?o - order ?a - attempt)    ; client is about to send attempt ?a for order ?o
    (waiting ?o - order ?a - attempt)  ; client sent attempt ?a and awaits the response
    (clock ?o - order ?t - tick)       ; client's timer for the outstanding attempt
    (confirmed ?o - order)             ; client received a success response
    ;; --- network ---
    (in-flight ?o - order ?a - attempt) ; request of attempt ?a travelling to the provider
    (response ?o - order)               ; success response travelling back to the client
    ;; --- provider ---
    (approved ?o - order ?a - attempt)  ; provider accepted attempt ?a and will charge it
    (no-record ?o - order)              ; no idempotency record (and no reservation) for ?o yet
    (record ?o - order)                 ; idempotency record for ?o stored
    (uncharged ?o - order)
    (charged ?o - order)                ; card charged once
    (charged-twice ?o - order))         ; card charged a second time (the violation)

  (:action send
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (ready ?o ?a) (first-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (ready ?o ?a)) (waiting ?o ?a) (in-flight ?o ?a) (clock ?o ?t)))
  (:action lose-request
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (in-flight ?o ?a)
    :effect (not (in-flight ?o ?a)))
  (:action accept-no-dedup
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-none) (in-flight ?o ?a))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action accept-new-atomic
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-atomic) (in-flight ?o ?a) (no-record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (not (no-record ?o)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action accept-new-racy
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-racy) (in-flight ?o ?a) (no-record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action replay-duplicate-atomic
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-atomic) (in-flight ?o ?a) (record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (response ?o)))
  (:action replay-duplicate-racy
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-racy) (in-flight ?o ?a) (record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (response ?o)))
  (:action charge
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (approved ?o ?a) (uncharged ?o))
    :effect (and (not (approved ?o ?a)) (not (uncharged ?o)) (not (no-record ?o))
                 (charged ?o) (record ?o) (response ?o)))
  (:action charge-again
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (approved ?o ?a) (charged ?o))
    :effect (and (not (approved ?o ?a)) (charged-twice ?o) (response ?o)))
  (:action lose-response
    :parameters (?o - order)
    :precondition (response ?o)
    :effect (not (response ?o)))
  (:action receive-response
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (waiting ?o ?a) (response ?o))
    :effect (and (not (waiting ?o ?a)) (not (response ?o)) (confirmed ?o)))
  (:action tick
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt ?t ?u - tick)
    :precondition (and (waiting ?o ?a) (clock ?o ?t) (next-tick ?t ?u))
    :effect (and (not (clock ?o ?t)) (clock ?o ?u)))
  (:action time-out-and-retry
    :parameters (?o - order ?a ?b - attempt ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (waiting ?o ?a) (clock ?o ?t) (timeout-tick ?t) (next-attempt ?a ?b))
    :effect (and (not (waiting ?o ?a)) (not (clock ?o ?t)) (ready ?o ?b))))
```

Object names: the order is o1; attempts are a0 (first try), a1 and a2 (retries); client timer values are t0 to t7.

Question: Can the customer's card be charged twice for order o1? In the event model this means reaching a state where (charged-twice o1) holds.

If it can happen, give a complete event sequence, starting from the initial situation described in
the design document, that ends in such a state: a list of ground actions such as "(action arg1 arg2)".
Every action's precondition must hold at the moment it occurs. If it cannot happen under this design,
say so.

End your answer with a JSON object in a ```json block, either
{"verdict": "violation", "trace": ["(action arg ...)", ...]}
or
{"verdict": "safe"}

completion.text:
**Verdict: safe.** Under the design's atomic-reservation mode, `(charged-twice o1)` is unreachable.

**Setup.** The design doc specifies an atomic insert-if-absent, so the mode is `(dedup-atomic)`. `dedup-none` and `dedup-racy` are false in every reachable state, because no action changes them. Initially `(no-record o1)`, `(uncharged o1)`, and `(ready o1 a0)` hold.

**What `charged-twice` needs.** Only `charge-again` produces it. Its precondition is `(approved o1 a)` and `(charged o1)` for some attempt `a`.

**Where `approved` can come from.** Three actions add `(approved o1 a)`:
- `accept-no-dedup` requires `(dedup-none)`, which is false.
- `accept-new-racy` requires `(dedup-racy)`, which is false.
- `accept-new-atomic` requires `(dedup-atomic)`, `(in-flight o1 a)` and `(no-record o1)`.

So only `accept-new-atomic` can approve a request. In the same step it deletes `(no-record o1)`.

**No-record never returns.** No action adds `(no-record o1)` back. `charge` and `accept-new-atomic` delete it, and nothing else touches it. So `accept-new-atomic` can fire at most once in any execution. That means at most one `(approved o1 ·)` fact is ever created.

**Charge and charge-again.** The single approval can be consumed in exactly one of two ways:
- `charge` consumes it, which needs `(uncharged o1)`. This produces `(charged o1)` and deletes the approval.
- `charge-again` would need `(charged o1)`. That is only true after a `charge`, which already consumed the one approval.

For `charge-again` to fire, a second approval would have to exist after `(charged o1)` is true. None can be created.

**Races, retries and delays.** These cannot break this argument:
- A delayed request from an earlier attempt, or a retry (a1, a2) that arrives later, finds `(no-record o1)` false.
- If `(record o1)` is true, it takes `replay-duplicate-atomic`, which only emits a response and causes no charge.
- If the first request is approved but not yet charged, so there is neither `no-record` nor `record`, the late request has no applicable accept action. It just stays in flight or is lost, so no charge happens.

The atomic reservation therefore makes the lookup and the insert a single step. This closes the window that the racy mode would leave open.

```json
{"verdict": "safe"}
```

prompt:
--- Design document ---
Product page cache (design doc)

Product details live in a database and are cached in a key-value cache using the cache-aside
pattern. One reader process serves product-page requests: on a cache hit it uses the cached value;
on a miss it reads the current value from the database and then stores what it read in the cache.
One writer process applies a batch of 1 price update to the product, one after another, moving
the database from version v0 to v1. Reader and writer steps interleave arbitrarily, and the reader
can be delayed for any amount of time between reading the database and storing into the cache.
Cache entries have no expiry time.

Writes. For each update the writer first writes the new version to the database and then deletes
the product's cache entry, so the next read misses and loads the new version. The reader always
stores the value it read after a miss.

Initially the database holds v0, the cache is empty, the reader is idle, and the writer is about to start its first update.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
(define (domain cache-aside)
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types version)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts (which of these hold depends on the design) ---
    (mode-4)
    (mode-3)
    (mode-2)
    (mode-1)
    ;; --- static ---
    (next-version ?v ?w - version) (older ?v ?w - version) (final-version ?v - version)
    ;; --- state ---
    (db ?v - version) (cache ?v - version) (cache-empty)
    (reader-idle) (reader-has ?v - version) (lease)
    (writer-start ?v - version)        ; writer is about to begin its updates (database at ?v)
    (writer-update ?v - version)       ; writer's next step: write the version after ?v to the database
    (writer-invalidate ?v - version)   ; writer's next step: delete the cache entry (database is at ?v)
    (writer-done)
    (stale))                           ; after the writer finished, the cache holds an older version than the database

  (:action read-miss
    :parameters (?v - version)
    :precondition (and (reader-idle) (cache-empty) (db ?v))
    :effect (and (not (reader-idle)) (reader-has ?v) (lease)))
  (:action fill-1
    :parameters (?v - version)
    :precondition (and (mode-2) (reader-has ?v) (cache-empty))
    :effect (and (not (reader-has ?v)) (not (cache-empty)) (cache ?v) (reader-idle)))
  (:action fill-2
    :parameters (?v - version)
    :precondition (and (mode-1) (reader-has ?v) (cache-empty) (lease))
    :effect (and (not (reader-has ?v)) (not (cache-empty)) (not (lease)) (cache ?v) (reader-idle)))
  (:action abandon-fill
    :parameters (?v - version)
    :precondition (reader-has ?v)
    :effect (and (not (reader-has ?v)) (reader-idle)))
  (:action begin-1
    :parameters (?v - version)
    :precondition (and (mode-4) (writer-start ?v))
    :effect (and (not (writer-start ?v)) (writer-update ?v)))
  (:action begin-2
    :parameters (?v - version)
    :precondition (and (mode-3) (writer-start ?v))
    :effect (and (not (writer-start ?v)) (writer-invalidate ?v)))
  (:action write-db
    :parameters (?v ?w - version)
    :precondition (and (writer-update ?v) (db ?v) (next-version ?v ?w))
    :effect (and (not (writer-update ?v)) (not (db ?v)) (db ?w) (writer-invalidate ?w)))
  (:action invalidate
    :parameters (?v ?x - version)
    :precondition (and (writer-invalidate ?v) (cache ?x))
    :effect (and (not (writer-invalidate ?v)) (not (cache ?x)) (not (lease)) (cache-empty) (writer-update ?v)))
  (:action invalidate-empty
    :parameters (?v - version)
    :precondition (and (writer-invalidate ?v) (cache-empty))
    :effect (and (not (writer-invalidate ?v)) (not (lease)) (writer-update ?v)))
  (:action finish-2
    :parameters (?v - version)
    :precondition (and (mode-4) (writer-update ?v) (final-version ?v))
    :effect (and (not (writer-update ?v)) (writer-done)))
  (:action finish-1
    :parameters (?v - version)
    :precondition (and (mode-3) (writer-invalidate ?v) (final-version ?v))
    :effect (and (not (writer-invalidate ?v)) (writer-done)))
  (:action observe-stale
    :parameters (?v ?w - version)
    :precondition (and (writer-done) (cache ?v) (db ?w) (older ?v ?w))
    :effect (stale)))
```

Object names: versions v0 (initial) to v1.

Question: Can the cache be left holding an older version than the database after the writer has finished all its updates? In the event model this means reaching a state where (stale) holds.

Do NOT try to answer the question yourself. Instead, write the PDDL problem file that encodes this
particular design: its objects, its complete initial state, and the goal. A classical planner will then
search it: complete forward search with the FF heuristic decides whether the goal is reachable, and
SATPlan returns the shortest event sequence that reaches it.

Requirements:
- use (:domain cache-aside) and the object names given above, each declared with its type;
- :init must list every fact that is true initially, including the design facts that describe this
  design and static facts such as counter successors (closed world: anything not listed is false);
- :goal must be (stale).

Answer with the problem in one ```pddl block.

completion.text:
```pddl
(define (problem cache-aside-v0-v1)
  (:domain cache-aside)
  (:objects v0 v1 - version)
  (:init
    ;; design facts: writer writes the database then invalidates (mode-4);
    ;; reader stores what it read without any lease check (mode-2)
    (mode-4)
    (mode-2)
    ;; static facts
    (next-version v0 v1)
    (older v0 v1)
    (final-version v1)

    (db v0)
    (cache-empty)
    (reader-idle)
    (writer-start v0))
```

prompt:
--- Design document ---
Report-generation job: leader lock design (design doc)

Two worker processes, c1 and c2, may both try to run the nightly job, which overwrites a shared file
in object storage. To make sure only one of them writes, a worker must first acquire a lock from the
lock service. The lock is a lease: it is granted for 5 clock ticks, after which the lock service
considers it expired and may grant it to the other worker. Each grant comes with a token from a
counter (k1 for the first grant, then k2, ...; k0 is the initial counter value and is never handed
out). Each worker writes the file at most once.

Workers can stall at any point for an unbounded time (garbage-collection pauses, VM migration,
slow network), and they learn nothing about lease expiry while stalled: a worker that has acquired
the lock keeps believing it holds it.

Writing. Once a worker holds the lock it writes the file. The storage service accepts any write;
the token is logged for auditing only.

Initially the lock is free, no token has been issued yet (the counter is at k0), the storage has seen token k0, and neither worker has acquired the lock.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
(define (domain lease-lock)
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types client tick token)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts (which of these hold depends on the design) ---
    (mode-3)
    (mode-2)
    (mode-1)
    (mode-4)
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick) (zero-tick ?t - tick)
    (lease-limit ?t - tick)              ; lease age at which the lock service expires the lease
    (next-token ?k ?l - token)           ; token ?l is issued after ?k
    (token-less ?k ?l - token)           ; ?k < ?l
    (token-leq ?k ?l - token)            ; ?k <= ?l
    ;; --- lock service ---
    (lock-free) (holder ?c - client) (lease-age ?t - tick) (last-issued ?k - token)
    ;; --- clients ---
    (idle ?c - client)                   ; has not acquired the lock yet
    (believes ?c - client)               ; client thinks it holds the lock
    (lease-expired ?c - client)          ; the service expired this client's lease
    (token-of ?c - client ?k - token)
    (may-write ?c - client)              ; client is about to write to storage
    ;; --- storage ---
    (max-seen ?k - token)                ; newest token storage has seen (used with mode-3)
    (wrote ?k - token)                   ; a write with token ?k was applied
    (corrupted))                         ; an older holder's write was applied after a newer holder's write

  (:action acquire
    :parameters (?c - client ?k ?l - token ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (idle ?c) (lock-free) (last-issued ?k) (next-token ?k ?l) (zero-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (idle ?c)) (not (lock-free)) (not (last-issued ?k)) (last-issued ?l)
                 (holder ?c) (believes ?c) (token-of ?c ?l) (lease-age ?t)))
  (:action tick
    :parameters (?t ?u - tick)
    :precondition (and (lease-age ?t) (next-tick ?t ?u))
    :effect (and (not (lease-age ?t)) (lease-age ?u)))
  (:action expire
    :parameters (?c - client ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (holder ?c) (lease-age ?t) (lease-limit ?t))
    :effect (and (not (holder ?c)) (not (lease-age ?t)) (lock-free) (lease-expired ?c)))
  (:action prepare-1
    :parameters (?c - client)
    :precondition (and (mode-4) (believes ?c))
    :effect (may-write ?c))
  (:action check-1
    :parameters (?c - client)
    :precondition (and (mode-1) (believes ?c) (holder ?c))
    :effect (may-write ?c))
```

**Assumptions.** The design says the storage accepts any write and logs the token for auditing only. A worker that believes it holds the lock just writes, with no holder check and no fencing check. I also take the lease limit to be t5, which matches the 5-tick lease.

1. c1 acquires the lock and gets token k1, with lease age t0.
2. Five ticks pass, taking the lease age from t0 to t5.
3. The lock service expires c1's lease. The lock is free again, but c1 is stalled and still has `believes`.

Yes, the payout can be performed twice. The in-memory dedup set is lost when the consumer crashes, and the queue still redelivers the message.

**Sequence of events**

1. `receive`: w1 takes m1, which becomes hidden at age t0.
2. `process-and-record-in-memory`: w1 calls the bank API (the payout is now done), adds m1 to its in-memory set, and is now `handled`. The ack has not happened yet.
3. `crash-restart-losing-memory`: w1 crashes before acking. The restart wipes the in-memory set, so `seen m1` is false and `not-seen m1` is true. w1 is idle again, but m1 is still in the queue and hidden.
4. `tick` ×3: the hidden age advances t0→t1→t2→t3 with no ack, so the visibility timeout is reached.
5. `reappear`: m1 becomes visible again.
6. `receive`: the restarted w1 receives m1 again, with the age reset to t0.
7. `process-again`: m1 is already processed and w1's memory no longer has it, so w1 pays out a second time. This gives `processed-twice m1`.

**Root cause:** the dedup record and the side effect are not atomic with the ack, and the dedup state lives in volatile process memory. A crash between the payout and the ack, followed by a visibility timeout, defeats the dedup. The fix is to record processed ids durably in the same transaction as the payout. Better still, pass an idempotency key (the message id) to the bank API.

```python
def weekday(day, month, year):

    0 = Saturday, 1 = Sunday, 2 = Monday, ..., 6 = Friday.

    if month < 3:
```

prompt:
--- Design document ---
Checkout payment flow (design doc)

When a customer places order o1, the checkout service (the client) sends a charge request to an
external payment provider and waits for the reply. The network between them is unreliable: a request
or a response can be lost, and messages can be delayed arbitrarily, so a request may still be in
transit after the client has stopped waiting for it. The provider serves requests concurrently on
several worker threads, in whatever order they arrive, so the steps of different requests (looking up
records, charging, writing records) can interleave.

Each request is one attempt (a0 for the first try). After sending an attempt the client starts a
timer at t0; every clock tick advances it by one, and when it reaches t1 (1 tick after sending)
without a response the client gives up on that attempt and retries with the next attempt number
(a1, then a2). At most two retries are made. If a success response arrives while the client is still
waiting, the order is confirmed and no further attempts are made.

Charging and duplicate protection. Every attempt for an order carries the same idempotency key
(derived from the order number). When a request arrives, the provider looks the key up and, in the
same atomic database operation, inserts a reservation if it is absent (an insert-if-absent with a
unique constraint). Only a request whose insert succeeded is approved and charged; when the charge
succeeds the reservation is completed with the stored response. A request whose key already has a
completed record gets the stored success response back without a new charge; a request that finds
only an unfinished reservation is not charged either.

Initially the client is about to send attempt a0 for order o1; nothing has been charged and the provider has no record for o1.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
(define (domain payments)
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types order attempt tick)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts (which of these hold depends on the design) ---
    (mode-1)
    (mode-3)
    (mode-2)
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-attempt ?a ?b - attempt)   ; attempt ?b is the retry that follows attempt ?a
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick)         ; timer value ?u follows ?t
    (first-tick ?t - tick)           ; timer value right after a request is sent
    (timeout-tick ?t - tick)         ; timer value at which the client gives up waiting
    ;; --- client ---
    (ready ?o - order ?a - attempt)    ; client is about to send attempt ?a for order ?o
    (waiting ?o - order ?a - attempt)  ; client sent attempt ?a and awaits the response
    (clock ?o - order ?t - tick)       ; client's timer for the outstanding attempt
    (confirmed ?o - order)             ; client received a success response
    ;; --- network ---
    (in-flight ?o - order ?a - attempt) ; request of attempt ?a travelling to the provider
    (response ?o - order)               ; success response travelling back to the client
    ;; --- provider ---
    (approved ?o - order ?a - attempt)  ; provider accepted attempt ?a and will charge it
    (no-record ?o - order)              ; no idempotency record (and no reservation) for ?o yet
    (record ?o - order)                 ; idempotency record for ?o stored
    (uncharged ?o - order)
    (charged ?o - order)                ; card charged once
    (charged-twice ?o - order))         ; card charged a second time (the violation)

  (:action send
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (ready ?o ?a) (first-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (ready ?o ?a)) (waiting ?o ?a) (in-flight ?o ?a) (clock ?o ?t)))
  (:action lose-request
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (in-flight ?o ?a)
    :effect (not (in-flight ?o ?a)))
  (:action accept-2
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (mode-1) (in-flight ?o ?a))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action accept-1
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (mode-3) (in-flight ?o ?a) (no-record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (not (no-record ?o)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action accept-3
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (mode-2) (in-flight ?o ?a) (no-record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action replay-2
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (mode-3) (in-flight ?o ?a) (record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (response ?o)))
  (:action replay-1
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (mode-2) (in-flight ?o ?a) (record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (response ?o)))
  (:action charge
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (approved ?o ?a) (uncharged ?o))
    :effect (and (not (approved ?o ?a)) (not (uncharged ?o)) (not (no-record ?o))
```

**Verdict: safe.** Under this design the card cannot be charged twice for o1.

**Which design facts hold.** The document says the provider does the key lookup and the reservation insert in one atomic insert-if-absent operation, and only a request whose insert succeeded is approved. That matches `mode-3`:
- `accept-1` requires `(no-record o1)` and removes it in the same step as approving the attempt. This is the atomic check-and-reserve.
- `replay-2` returns the stored response when a completed `record` exists, with no new charge.

The `mode-1` actions (no dedupe check) and `mode-2` actions (check without reserving) are not enabled by this design.

**Why `charged-twice` is unreachable.**
1. `charged-twice o1` is only produced by `charge-again`, which needs `(approved o1 a)` and `(charged o1)` at the same time.
2. `approved o1 _` is only produced by `accept-1`, which needs `(no-record o1)` and deletes it.
3. No action ever re-adds `no-record o1`. The `charge` action only deletes it, so it is false from the first approval onward.

Two worker processes, c1 and c2, may both try to run the nightly job, which overwrites a shared file
in object storage. To make sure only one of them writes, a worker must first acquire a lock from the
lock service. The lock is a lease: it is granted for 1 clock tick, after which the lock service
considers it expired and may grant it to the other worker. Each grant comes with a token from a
counter (k1 for the first grant, then k2, ...; k0 is the initial counter value and is never handed
out). Each worker writes the file at most once.

Workers can stall at any point for an unbounded time (garbage-collection pauses, VM migration,
slow network), and they learn nothing about lease expiry while stalled: a worker that has acquired
the lock keeps believing it holds it.

Writing. Right before writing, the worker asks the lock service whether it still holds an unexpired
lease, and writes only if the answer is yes. Every write carries the worker's token, and the storage
service remembers the highest token it has accepted: it rejects any write whose token is lower than
that (fencing), and accepts and records the others.

Initially the lock is free, no token has been issued yet (the counter is at k0), the storage has seen token k0, and neither worker has acquired the lock.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
(define (domain lease-lock)
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types client tick token)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts (which of these hold depends on the design) ---
    (mode-3)
    (mode-2)
    (mode-1)
    (mode-4)
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick) (zero-tick ?t - tick)
    (lease-limit ?t - tick)              ; lease age at which the lock service expires the lease
    (next-token ?k ?l - token)           ; token ?l is issued after ?k
    (token-less ?k ?l - token)           ; ?k < ?l
    (token-leq ?k ?l - token)            ; ?k <= ?l
    ;; --- lock service ---
    (lock-free) (holder ?c - client) (lease-age ?t - tick) (last-issued ?k - token)
    ;; --- clients ---
    (idle ?c - client)                   ; has not acquired the lock yet
    (believes ?c - client)               ; client thinks it holds the lock
    (lease-expired ?c - client)          ; the service expired this client's lease
    (token-of ?c - client ?k - token)
    (may-write ?c - client)              ; client is about to write to storage
    ;; --- storage ---
    (max-seen ?k - token)
    (wrote ?k - token)                   ; a write with token ?k was applied
    (corrupted))                         ; an older holder's write was applied after a newer holder's write

  (:action acquire
    :parameters (?c - client ?k ?l - token ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (idle ?c) (lock-free) (last-issued ?k) (next-token ?k ?l) (zero-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (idle ?c)) (not (lock-free)) (not (last-issued ?k)) (last-issued ?l)
                 (holder ?c) (believes ?c) (token-of ?c ?l) (lease-age ?t)))
  (:action tick
    :parameters (?t ?u - tick)
    :precondition (and (lease-age ?t) (next-tick ?t ?u))
    :effect (and (not (lease-age ?t)) (lease-age ?u)))
  (:action expire
    :parameters (?c - client ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (holder ?c) (lease-age ?t) (lease-limit ?t))
    :effect (and (not (holder ?c)) (not (lease-age ?t)) (lock-free) (lease-expired ?c)))
  (:action prepare-1
    :parameters (?c - client)
    :precondition (and (mode-4) (believes ?c))
    :effect (may-write ?c))
  (:action check-1
    :parameters (?c - client)
    :precondition (and (mode-1) (believes ?c) (holder ?c))
    :effect (may-write ?c))
  (:action write-4
    :parameters (?c - client ?k - token)
    :precondition (and (mode-2) (may-write ?c) (token-of ?c ?k))
    :effect (and (not (may-write ?c)) (not (believes ?c)) (wrote ?k)))
  (:action write-1
    :parameters (?c - client ?k ?m - token)
    :precondition (and (mode-2) (may-write ?c) (token-of ?c ?k) (wrote ?m) (token-less ?k ?m))
    :effect (and (not (may-write ?c)) (not (believes ?c)) (corrupted)))
  (:action write-3
    :parameters (?c - client ?k ?j - token)
    :precondition (and (mode-3) (may-write ?c) (token-of ?c ?k) (max-seen ?j) (token-leq ?j ?k))
    :effect (and (not (may-write ?c)) (not (believes ?c)) (not (max-seen ?j)) (max-seen ?k) (wrote ?k)))
  (:action write-2
    :parameters (?c - client ?k ?j ?m - token)
    :precondition (and (mode-3) (may-write ?c) (token-of ?c ?k) (max-seen ?j) (token-leq ?j ?k)
                       (wrote ?m) (token-less ?k ?m))
    :effect (and (not (may-write ?c)) (not (believes ?c)) (corrupted)))
  (:action reject-1
    :parameters (?c - client ?k ?j - token)
    :precondition (and (mode-3) (may-write ?c) (token-of ?c ?k) (max-seen ?j) (token-less ?k ?j))
    :effect (and (not (may-write ?c)) (not (believes ?c)))))
```

Object names: clients c1 and c2; lease ages t0 to t1; tokens k0 (initial value, never handed out) to k3.

Question: Can a write from a worker whose lease had expired be applied after the other worker's write (corrupting the file)? In the event model this means reaching a state where (corrupted) holds.

If it can happen, give a complete event sequence, starting from the initial situation described in
the design document, that ends in such a state: a list of ground actions such as "(action arg1 arg2)".
Every action's precondition must hold at the moment it occurs. If it cannot happen under this design,
say so.

End your answer with a JSON object in a ```json block, either
{"verdict": "violation", "trace": ["(action arg ...)", ...]}
or
{"verdict": "safe"}

completion.text:
**Verdict: safe.** No event sequence reaches `(corrupted)` under this design.

**Which modes are active.** The design has two write-time protections, and each maps to one mode:
- The lease check right before writing is `check-1`, which needs `mode-1`.
- Storage fencing is `write-3`, `write-2` and `reject-1`, which need `mode-3`.

So `mode-1` and `mode-3` hold. `mode-2` (unfenced writes) and `mode-4` (no lease check) do not hold. That means `write-4`, `write-1` and `prepare-1` can never fire.

**Why `corrupted` is unreachable.** The only remaining action that sets `corrupted` is `write-2`. Its precondition requires all of the following:
- `(max-seen j)` with `j ≤ k`, where `k` is the writer's token.
- `(wrote m)` for some `m` with `k < m`.

Two invariants rule this out:
1. The only action that adds `wrote m` is `write-3`. It also sets `max-seen m` in the same step. So whenever `wrote m` holds, `max-seen` is at least `m`.
2. `max-seen` never decreases. `write-3` replaces `j` with `k` only when `j ≤ k`, and `reject-1` and `write-2` leave it unchanged.

Suppose `wrote m` holds. Then `max-seen j` implies `j ≥ m`. But `write-2` needs `j ≤ k < m`, which contradicts `j ≥ m`. So `write-2` can never fire.

A stalled worker with an expired lease and a lower token takes the `reject-1` path instead. That path clears `may-write` and `believes` and does not corrupt anything.

The lease check (`check-1`) is only racy, since a worker can stall after the check. Fencing at the storage service is what makes the design safe.


prompt:
--- Design document ---
Checkout payment flow (design doc)

When a customer places order o1, the checkout service (the client) sends a charge request to an
external payment provider and waits for the reply. The network between them is unreliable: a request
or a response can be lost, and messages can be delayed arbitrarily, so a request may still be in
transit after the client has stopped waiting for it. The provider handles requests one at a time,
in whatever order they arrive.

Each request is one attempt (a0 for the first try). After sending an attempt the client starts a
timer at t0; every clock tick advances it by one, and when it reaches t11 (11 ticks after sending)
without a response the client gives up on that attempt and retries with the next attempt number
(a1, then a2). At most two retries are made. If a success response arrives while the client is still
waiting, the order is confirmed and no further attempts are made.

Charging and duplicate protection. Every attempt for an order carries the same idempotency key
(derived from the order number). When a request arrives, the provider looks the key up in its
idempotency table. If a record is found, the provider does not charge again; it just returns the
stored success response. If no record is found, the provider approves the request, charges the card,
and, once the charge has succeeded, writes the record for the key together with the response.

Initially the client is about to send attempt a0 for order o1; nothing has been charged and the provider has no record for o1.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
(define (domain payments)
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types order attempt tick)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts: exactly one deduplication mode holds ---
    (dedup-none)     ; the provider does not deduplicate requests
    (dedup-atomic)   ; the provider looks up and reserves the idempotency key in one atomic step
    (dedup-racy)     ; the provider looks up the key, but only records it after the charge succeeds
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-attempt ?a ?b - attempt)   ; attempt ?b is the retry that follows attempt ?a
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick)         ; timer value ?u follows ?t
    (first-tick ?t - tick)           ; timer value right after a request is sent
    (timeout-tick ?t - tick)         ; timer value at which the client gives up waiting
    ;; --- client ---
    (ready ?o - order ?a - attempt)    ; client is about to send attempt ?a for order ?o
    (waiting ?o - order ?a - attempt)  ; client sent attempt ?a and awaits the response
    (clock ?o - order ?t - tick)       ; client's timer for the outstanding attempt
    (confirmed ?o - order)             ; client received a success response
    ;; --- network ---
    (in-flight ?o - order ?a - attempt) ; request of attempt ?a travelling to the provider
    (response ?o - order)               ; success response travelling back to the client
    ;; --- provider ---
    (approved ?o - order ?a - attempt)  ; provider accepted attempt ?a and will charge it
    (no-record ?o - order)              ; no idempotency record (and no reservation) for ?o yet
    (record ?o - order)                 ; idempotency record for ?o stored
    (uncharged ?o - order)
    (charged ?o - order)                ; card charged once
    (charged-twice ?o - order))         ; card charged a second time (the violation)

  (:action send
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (ready ?o ?a) (first-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (ready ?o ?a)) (waiting ?o ?a) (in-flight ?o ?a) (clock ?o ?t)))
  (:action lose-request
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (in-flight ?o ?a)
    :effect (not (in-flight ?o ?a)))
  (:action accept-no-dedup
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-none) (in-flight ?o ?a))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action accept-new-atomic
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-atomic) (in-flight ?o ?a) (no-record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (not (no-record ?o)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action accept-new-racy
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-racy) (in-flight ?o ?a) (no-record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action replay-duplicate-atomic
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-atomic) (in-flight ?o ?a) (record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (response ?o)))
  (:action replay-duplicate-racy
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-racy) (in-flight ?o ?a) (record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (response ?o)))
  (:action charge
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (approved ?o ?a) (uncharged ?o))
    :effect (and (not (approved ?o ?a)) (not (uncharged ?o)) (not (no-record ?o))
                 (charged ?o) (record ?o) (response ?o)))
  (:action charge-again
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (approved ?o ?a) (charged ?o))
    :effect (and (not (approved ?o ?a)) (charged-twice ?o) (response ?o)))
  (:action lose-response
    :parameters (?o - order)
    :precondition (response ?o)
    :effect (not (response ?o)))
  (:action receive-response
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (waiting ?o ?a) (response ?o))
    :effect (and (not (waiting ?o ?a)) (not (response ?o)) (confirmed ?o)))
  (:action tick
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt ?t ?u - tick)
    :precondition (and (waiting ?o ?a) (clock ?o ?t) (next-tick ?t ?u))
    :effect (and (not (clock ?o ?t)) (clock ?o ?u)))
  (:action time-out-and-retry
    :parameters (?o - order ?a ?b - attempt ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (waiting ?o ?a) (clock ?o ?t) (timeout-tick ?t) (next-attempt ?a ?b))
    :effect (and (not (waiting ?o ?a)) (not (clock ?o ?t)) (ready ?o ?b))))
```

prompt:
--- Design document ---
Payout worker: queue consumer design (design doc)

When a seller's balance is settled, a "send payout" message (m1) is put on a message queue. A
consumer process (w1) receives messages from the queue and, for each one, performs the payout by
crediting the amount to the seller's wallet balance, which is stored in the payments database (a
credit, once committed, is not reversed automatically), then acknowledges the message so the queue
deletes it.

The queue guarantees at-least-once delivery. A received message is hidden from consumers; if it is
not acknowledged within 5 clock ticks of being received (the visibility timeout) it becomes visible
again and will be delivered again. The consumer process can crash at any moment and is restarted
automatically, after which it continues receiving messages.

Processing and deduplication. The consumer keeps the ids of messages it has already paid out in a
set in its process memory. Before performing a payout it checks the set: if the id is there it skips
the payout and only acknowledges the message; otherwise it credits the wallet, adds the id to the
set, and acknowledges.

Initially m1 is in the queue and visible, nothing has been paid out, and w1 is idle.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
(define (domain queue)
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types message consumer tick)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts: exactly one deduplication mode holds ---
    (dedup-none)      ; the consumer processes every delivery
    (dedup-durable)   ; processed ids are recorded in the database, atomically with the side effect
    (dedup-memory)    ; processed ids are recorded in an in-memory set of the consumer process
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick) (zero-tick ?t - tick)
    (visibility-timeout ?t - tick)        ; age at which an unacknowledged message becomes visible again
    ;; --- queue ---
    (in-queue ?m - message) (visible ?m - message) (hidden ?m - message ?t - tick) (acked ?m - message)
    ;; --- consumer ---
    (idle ?w - consumer) (working ?w - consumer ?m - message) (handled ?w - consumer ?m - message)
    ;; --- effects of processing ---
    (unprocessed ?m - message) (processed ?m - message) (processed-twice ?m - message)
    (not-seen ?m - message) (seen ?m - message))

  (:action receive
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (idle ?w) (visible ?m) (in-queue ?m) (zero-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (idle ?w)) (not (visible ?m)) (working ?w ?m) (hidden ?m ?t)))
  (:action process-without-dedup
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (dedup-none) (working ?w ?m) (unprocessed ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (not (unprocessed ?m)) (processed ?m) (handled ?w ?m)))
  (:action process-and-record-durably
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (dedup-durable) (working ?w ?m) (unprocessed ?m) (not-seen ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (not (unprocessed ?m)) (not (not-seen ?m)) (seen ?m)
                 (processed ?m) (handled ?w ?m)))
  (:action process-and-record-in-memory
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (dedup-memory) (working ?w ?m) (unprocessed ?m) (not-seen ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (not (unprocessed ?m)) (not (not-seen ?m)) (seen ?m)
                 (processed ?m) (handled ?w ?m)))
  (:action skip-duplicate
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (working ?w ?m) (seen ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (handled ?w ?m)))
  (:action process-again
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (working ?w ?m) (processed ?m) (not-seen ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (processed-twice ?m) (handled ?w ?m)))
  (:action ack
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (handled ?w ?m) (hidden ?m ?t))
    :effect (and (not (handled ?w ?m)) (not (hidden ?m ?t)) (not (in-queue ?m)) (idle ?w) (acked ?m)))
  (:action tick
    :parameters (?m - message ?t ?u - tick)
    :precondition (and (hidden ?m ?t) (next-tick ?t ?u))
    :effect (and (not (hidden ?m ?t)) (hidden ?m ?u)))
  (:action reappear
    :parameters (?m - message ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (hidden ?m ?t) (visibility-timeout ?t) (in-queue ?m))
    :effect (and (not (hidden ?m ?t)) (visible ?m)))
  (:action crash-restart
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (handled ?w ?m)
    :effect (and (not (handled ?w ?m)) (idle ?w)))
  (:action crash-restart-losing-memory
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (dedup-memory) (handled ?w ?m) (seen ?m))
    :effect (and (not (handled ?w ?m)) (not (seen ?m)) (not-seen ?m) (idle ?w))))
```

--- Design document ---
Checkout payment flow (design doc)

When a customer places order o1, the checkout service (the client) sends a charge request to an
external payment provider and waits for the reply. The network between them is unreliable: a request
or a response can be lost, and messages can be delayed arbitrarily, so a request may still be in
transit after the client has stopped waiting for it. The provider serves requests concurrently on
several worker threads, in whatever order they arrive, so the steps of different requests (looking up
records, charging, writing records) can interleave.

Each request is one attempt (a0 for the first try). After sending an attempt the client starts a
timer at t0; every clock tick advances it by one, and when it reaches t31 (31 ticks after sending)
without a response the client gives up on that attempt and retries with the next attempt number
(a1, then a2). At most two retries are made. If a success response arrives while the client is still
waiting, the order is confirmed and no further attempts are made.

Charging and duplicate protection. Every attempt for an order carries the same idempotency key
(derived from the order number). When a request arrives, the provider looks the key up and, in the
same atomic database operation, inserts a reservation if it is absent (an insert-if-absent with a
unique constraint). Only a request whose insert succeeded is approved and charged; when the charge
succeeds the reservation is completed with the stored response. A request whose key already has a
completed record gets the stored success response back without a new charge; a request that finds
only an unfinished reservation is not charged either.

Initially the client is about to send attempt a0 for order o1; nothing has been charged and the provider has no record for o1.

--- Event model ---

is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types order attempt tick)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts: exactly one deduplication mode holds ---
    (dedup-none)     ; the provider does not deduplicate requests
    (dedup-atomic)   ; the provider looks up and reserves the idempotency key in one atomic step
    (dedup-racy)     ; the provider looks up the key, but only records it after the charge succeeds
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-attempt ?a ?b - attempt)   ; attempt ?b is the retry that follows attempt ?a
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick)         ; timer value ?u follows ?t
    (first-tick ?t - tick)           ; timer value right after a request is sent
    (timeout-tick ?t - tick)         ; timer value at which the client gives up waiting
    ;; --- client ---

    (waiting ?o - order ?a - attempt)  ; client sent attempt ?a and awaits the response
    (clock ?o - order ?t - tick)       ; client's timer for the outstanding attempt
    (confirmed ?o - order)             ; client received a success response
    ;; --- network ---
```

completion.text:
**Verdict: safe.** Under the stated design, the mode is `dedup-atomic`, and `(charged-twice o1)` is unreachable.

**Why it can't happen**

1. `charged-twice` is only produced by `charge-again`. That action needs `(approved o1 a)` and `(charged o1)` to hold together.
2. `charged` is only produced by `charge`, which consumes one `approved` fact. So for a second charge, a second `approved` fact must exist after the first charge has run, or at least alongside it.
3. With `dedup-atomic`, `approved` can only be created by `accept-new-atomic`. Its precondition is `(no-record o1)`, and its effect deletes `no-record o1` in the same step.
4. Nothing ever re-adds `no-record o1`. It is true only in the initial state, so `accept-new-atomic` can fire at most once. The other approval actions need a different mode: `accept-no-dedup` needs `dedup-none` and `accept-new-racy` needs `dedup-racy`. Neither mode holds, and no action changes the mode.
5. So at most one `approved o1 _` fact ever exists. After `charge` consumes it, no `approved` fact remains for `charge-again` to use.

**Retries and delays don't change this**

- Timeouts can create a1 and a2 while a0 is still in transit, and requests can be lost, delayed or reordered.
- A later request sees either an unfinished reservation or a completed record. With an unfinished reservation (`no-record` false, `record` false), no action applies to it, so it is simply never charged. With a completed record, `replay-duplicate-atomic` only produces a `response`, with no charge.
- The worst case is a lost response or a stuck request, which hurts liveness (the customer may not get confirmation) but not safety.

The race in the design would only exist in `dedup-racy` mode, where `no-record` stays true until after the charge. That is not the mode this document specifies.

--- Design document ---
Product page cache (design doc)

Product details live in a database and are cached in a key-value cache using the cache-aside
pattern. One reader process serves product-page requests: on a cache hit it uses the cached value;
on a miss it reads the current value from the database and then stores what it read in the cache.
One writer process applies a batch of 1 price update to the product, one after another, moving
the database from version v0 to v1. Reader and writer steps interleave arbitrarily, and the reader
can be delayed for any amount of time between reading the database and storing into the cache.
Cache entries have no expiry time.

Writes. For each update the writer first writes the new version to the database and then deletes
the product's cache entry, so the next read misses and loads the new version. The reader always
stores the value it read after a miss.

Initially the database holds v0, the cache is empty, the reader is idle, and the writer is about to start its first update.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
(define (domain cache-aside)
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types version)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts ---
    (update-then-delete)   ; the writer updates the database, then deletes the cache entry
    (delete-then-update)   ; the writer deletes the cache entry, then updates the database
    (plain-set)            ; a reader that missed always stores the value it read
    (leased-set)           ; a reader may store its value only if its lease was not revoked by a delete
    ;; --- static ---
    (next-version ?v ?w - version) (older ?v ?w - version) (final-version ?v - version)
    ;; --- state ---
    (db ?v - version) (cache ?v - version) (cache-empty)
    (reader-idle) (reader-has ?v - version) (lease)
    (writer-start ?v - version)        ; writer is about to begin its updates (database at ?v)
    (writer-update ?v - version)       ; writer's next step: write the version after ?v to the database
    (writer-invalidate ?v - version)   ; writer's next step: delete the cache entry (database is at ?v)
    (writer-done)
    (stale))                           ; after the writer finished, the cache holds an older version than the database

  (:action read-miss
```

**Yes, the cache can end up stale.** The race is the classic cache-aside one: the reader's read of the database and its store into the cache are separate steps, and the writer's delete can fall between them.

transaction, so either both are stored or neither is (a crash before the commit rolls both back).

Question: Can the payout for message m1 be performed twice? In the event model this means reaching a state where (processed-twice m1) holds.

If it can happen, give a complete event sequence, starting from the initial situation described in
the design document, that ends in such a state: a list of ground actions such as "(action arg1 arg2)".

completion.text:
**Verdict: safe.** Under this design, `(processed-twice m1)` cannot be reached.

**Which mode holds.** The design records processed ids in the payments database, in the same transaction as the wallet credit. That is `dedup-durable`. The model's other modes (`dedup-none` and `dedup-memory`) don't hold, so their actions are disabled.

**The only way to get `processed-twice`.** `process-again` is the only action that adds it. It needs `(working w1 m1)`, `(processed m1)` and `(not-seen m1)` to hold together.

**Why those preconditions can't hold together:**
1. Initially `processed m1` is false and `not-seen m1` is true. The first payout can only happen through `process-and-record-durably`.
2. That action makes `processed m1` true and `not-seen m1` false, and it makes `seen m1` true. It does all of this in one step, which models the credit and the id record committing in a single transaction.
3. Nothing restores `not-seen m1` afterwards. The only action that does is `crash-restart-losing-memory`, and it requires `dedup-memory`, which is false here.
4. `crash-restart` only clears `handled` and sets `idle`. It leaves `seen` and `processed` untouched, because the database record survives a crash.
5. A crash before the commit means `process-and-record-durably` never happened, so there is no credit and no record. The next delivery is then the first payout, not a second one.

So `processed m1` and `not-seen m1` are never true at the same time, and `process-again` can never fire.

**Redelivery cases.**
- If the visibility timeout expires while w1 is still working, `reappear` makes m1 visible again. w1 cannot `receive` until it is idle.
- Every later delivery after a payout finds `seen m1` true. Only `skip-duplicate` is enabled, and it pays nothing.

At-least-once redelivery can still cause repeated deliveries or an ack that fails after the message reappears. Those affect liveness and efficiency, not the "paid at most once" requirement.

prompt:
--- Design document ---
Product page cache (design doc)

Product details live in a database and are cached in a key-value cache using the cache-aside
pattern. One reader process serves product-page requests: on a cache hit it uses the cached value;
on a miss it reads the current value from the database and then stores what it read in the cache.
One writer process applies a batch of 8 price updates to the product, one after another, moving
the database from version v0 to v8. Reader and writer steps interleave arbitrarily, and the reader
can be delayed for any amount of time between reading the database and storing into the cache.
Cache entries have no expiry time.

Writes. For each update the writer first writes the new version to the database and then deletes
the product's cache entry. On a miss the reader receives a lease token from the cache; a delete of
the entry revokes any outstanding lease, and the cache only accepts a store from a reader whose
lease is still valid (otherwise the reader drops its value).

Initially the database holds v0, the cache is empty, the reader is idle, and the writer is about to start its first update.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
(define (domain cache-aside)
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types version)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts ---
    (update-then-delete)   ; the writer updates the database, then deletes the cache entry
    (delete-then-update)   ; the writer deletes the cache entry, then updates the database
    (plain-set)            ; a reader that missed always stores the value it read
    (leased-set)           ; a reader may store its value only if its lease was not revoked by a delete
    ;; --- static ---
    (next-version ?v ?w - version) (older ?v ?w - version) (final-version ?v - version)
    ;; --- state ---
    (db ?v - version) (cache ?v - version) (cache-empty)
    (reader-idle) (reader-has ?v - version) (lease)
    (writer-start ?v - version)        ; writer is about to begin its updates (database at ?v)
    (writer-update ?v - version)       ; writer's next step: write the version after ?v to the database
    (writer-invalidate ?v - version)   ; writer's next step: delete the cache entry (database is at ?v)
    (writer-done)
    (stale))                           ; after the writer finished, the cache holds an older version than the database

  (:action read-miss
```

Yes, the design allows this. The reserve step is a read followed by a separate write, with no lock or transaction around it, and that permits a lost update.

**Which design facts hold.** The design describes the non-atomic reserve (read, then write `count-1`), so `mode-1` holds. It does not describe an atomic reserve, so `mode-4` does not. 3. c2, c3 and c4 each write 2, overwriting 2 with 2, and each holds a unit.

--- Design document ---
Checkout payment flow (design doc)

When a customer places order o1, the checkout service (the client) sends a charge request to an
external payment provider and waits for the reply. The network between them is unreliable: a request
or a response can be lost, and messages can be delayed arbitrarily, so a request may still be in
transit after the client has stopped waiting for it. The provider serves requests concurrently on
several worker threads, in whatever order they arrive, so the steps of different requests (looking up
records, charging, writing records) can interleave.

Each request is one attempt (a0 for the first try). After sending an attempt the client starts a
timer at t0; every clock tick advances it by one, and when it reaches t5 (5 ticks after sending)
without a response the client gives up on that attempt and retries with the next attempt number
(a1, then a2). At most two retries are made. If a success response arrives while the client is still
waiting, the order is confirmed and no further attempts are made.

Charging and duplicate protection. Every attempt for an order carries the same idempotency key
(derived from the order number). When a request arrives, the provider looks the key up and, in the
same atomic database operation, inserts a reservation if it is absent (an insert-if-absent with a
unique constraint). Only a request whose insert succeeded is approved and charged; when the charge
succeeds the reservation is completed with the stored response. A request whose key already has a
completed record gets the stored success response back without a new charge; a request that finds
only an unfinished reservation is not charged either.

Question: Can the customer's card be charged twice for order o1? In the event model this means reaching a state where (charged-twice o1) holds.

If it can happen, give a complete event sequence, starting from the initial situation described in
the design document, that ends in such a state: a list of ground actions such as "(action arg1 arg2)".

completion.text:
**Verdict: safe.** Under the design as written (the provider reserves the idempotency key atomically), no event sequence reaches `(charged-twice o1)`.

**Why a second charge is impossible**

1. `charged-twice` is produced only by `charge-again`. That action needs `(approved o1 ?a)` and `(charged o1)`. Since `charged` comes only from `charge`, which consumes an earlier approval, a second charge needs a second approval of o1 after the first.
2. The design fixes the mode as `dedup-atomic`, so `dedup-none` and `dedup-racy` are false. That disables `accept-no-dedup` and `accept-new-racy`, the two actions that could approve without consuming the reservation.
3. The only remaining way to get `approved` is `accept-new-atomic`. It requires `(no-record o1)` and, in the same step, deletes it.
4. Nothing ever re-adds `no-record o1`. `charge` only deletes it, and no other action sets it. So `accept-new-atomic` can fire at most once for o1, and at most one `approved o1 ?a` fact is ever created.
5. That single approval is consumed by `charge`, which makes `charged` true. After that no approval is left for `charge-again` to use.
6. A retry (a1 or a2) that arrives while the first attempt is in progress or after it finishes cannot be approved. Its `accept-new-atomic` is blocked because `no-record` is already false. It can only be handled by `replay-duplicate-atomic` if a record exists, which yields a response with no charge. Otherwise it stays in flight or is lost, which is the "unfinished reservation is not charged" case. Retries after timeouts, delayed requests and lost responses therefore cannot cause a double charge.

The race that would cause a double charge exists only in the `dedup-racy` variant, where the key is recorded after the charge and two workers can both pass the lookup. The atomic insert-if-absent in this design removes it.

```pddl
    (stock-atomic)      ; checkout decrements stock with one atomic conditional update

    (pay-ignores-hold)  ; payment is accepted even after the hold has expired

    :effect (and (not (read-stock ?c ?q)) (not (stock ?cur)) (stock ?p) (holding ?c) (hold-age ?c ?t)))

    :effect (and (not (hold-age ?c ?t)) (hold-age ?c ?u)))
```

**Yes, this can happen.** Two parts of the design combine to cause it:

- **Expired holds can still be paid.** The payment service looks the order up by customer id and never checks whether the hold is still active. This is the `pay-1` event, available when `mode-2` holds and the customer's hold has already expired.
- **The unit returns to stock on expiry.** Once c1's hold expires, the unit is back in stock, so c2 can reserve it with the atomic update. The atomic update itself is correct (`mode-4`), but it can't prevent this.

Event sequence:

1. `(reserve-1 c1 q1 q0 t0)`: c1 takes the only unit, so stock goes to 0 and c1 holds it at age 0.
2. `(hold-ages c1 t0 t1)`: one clock tick passes, and c1's hold reaches the expiry age.
3. `(expire-hold c1 t1 q0 q1)`: c1's hold expires and the unit goes back to stock (stock 1), with c1 marked `expired`.
4. `(reserve-1 c2 q1 q0 t0)`: c2 reserves the returned unit (stock 0).
5. `(pay c2 t0)`: c2 pays, and c2's purchase is confirmed.
6. `(pay-1 c1)`: c1 finally pays. The payment service doesn't check expiry, so c1's purchase is also confirmed.

The result is `(sold c1)` and `(sold c2)` with only 1 unit in stock, so the item is oversold.

--- Design document ---
Payout worker: queue consumer design (design doc)

When a seller's balance is settled, a "send payout" message (m1) is put on a message queue. A
consumer process (w1) receives messages from the queue and, for each one, performs the payout by
crediting the amount to the seller's wallet balance, which is stored in the payments database (a
credit, once committed, is not reversed automatically), then acknowledges the message so the queue
deletes it.

The queue guarantees at-least-once delivery. A received message is hidden from consumers; if it is
not acknowledged within 7 clock ticks of being received (the visibility timeout) it becomes visible
again and will be delivered again. The consumer process can crash at any moment and is restarted
automatically, after which it continues receiving messages.

Processing and deduplication. The consumer records the ids of messages it has already paid out in a
table in the payments database. The wallet credit and the id record are written in the same database
transaction, so either both are stored or neither is (a crash before the commit rolls both back).
Before performing a payout the consumer checks the table: if the id is there it skips the payout and
only acknowledges the message.

Initially m1 is in the queue and visible, nothing has been paid out, and w1 is idle.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types message consumer tick)

    (mode-2)
    (mode-1)
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick) (zero-tick ?t - tick)
    (visibility-timeout ?t - tick)        ; age at which an unacknowledged message becomes visible again
    ;; --- queue ---
    (in-queue ?m - message) (visible ?m - message) (hidden ?m - message ?t - tick) (acked ?m - message)
    ;; --- consumer ---
    (idle ?w - consumer) (working ?w - consumer ?m - message) (handled ?w - consumer ?m - message)
    ;; --- effects of processing ---
    (unprocessed ?m - message) (processed ?m - message) (processed-twice ?m - message)
    (not-seen ?m - message) (seen ?m - message))

    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (idle ?w) (visible ?m) (in-queue ?m) (zero-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (idle ?w)) (not (visible ?m)) (working ?w ?m) (hidden ?m ?t)))
  (:action process-2
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (mode-3) (working ?w ?m) (unprocessed ?m))
```
